## 3. Source tables

| Marker | Physical table (source `ic`) | Role |
|---|---|---|
| `{{TBL_AMS_LOT}}` | `"MFGA_INFOCENTRE"."DWH"."AMS_LOT"` | Lots (one lot = one accounting run of a fund on a NAV date) |
| `{{TBL_AMS_CASH_MVT}}` | `"MFGA_INFOCENTRE"."DWH"."AMS_CASH_MVT"` | Accounting entries (the ledger lines) |
| `{{TBL_AMS_PORTFOLIO}}` | `"MFGA_INFOCENTRE"."DWH"."AMS_PORTFOLIO"` | Fund / lot attributes (chart of accounts of the fund) |
| `{{TBL_AMS_ACC_DEF}}` | `"MFGA_INFOCENTRE"."DWH"."AMS_ACC_DEF"` | Account definitions / names |
| `{{TBL_AMS_ACC_POS}}` | `"MFGA_INFOCENTRE"."DWH"."AMS_ACC_POS"` | Account positions after each lot (final-balance control) |
| `{{TBL_TFM}}` | `"LUXIS"."REPADMIN"."TAB_FND_MAIN"` | "Table Fonds": fund name, currency, eFront flag, backdated-NAV flag |
| `{{TBL_NAV}}` | `"LUXIS"."REPADMIN"."NAV"` | LUXIS NAV table (first NAV with shares; controlled / published flags) |

Columns read, by table:

| Table | Columns |
|---|---|
| `AMS_LOT` | `C_FUND`, `N_LOT`, `D_NAV`, `D_H_PROCESS` |
| `AMS_CASH_MVT` | `C_FUND`, `N_LOT`, `N_LINE`, `N_ENTRY`, `N_ENTRY_PTF`, `N_NEXT`, `D_ACC`, `D_TRADE`, `D_VALUE`, `D_MATURITY`, `C_N_ACC`, `N_SUF`, `C_CCY`, `C_ACC_WAY` (`CR`/`DB`), `C_SRV`, `C_OPE`, `L_MVT`, `A_MVT`, `A_MVT_PTF`, `A_BALANCE`, `C_STATUS`, `C_N_PTF_MANAGER`, `R_EXCHANGE` |
| `AMS_PORTFOLIO` | `C_FUND`, `N_LOT`, `C_ACC_PLAN` |
| `AMS_ACC_DEF` | `C_N_ACC`, `L_NAME`, `N_LOT`, `C_ACC_PLAN` |
| `AMS_ACC_POS` | `C_FUND`, `N_LOT`, `C_N_ACC`, `N_SUF`, `C_ACC_CCY`, `D_MATURITY`, `C_N_PTF_MANAGER`, `A_BALANCE` |
| `TAB_FND_MAIN` | `FA_NUM`, `FUND_NAME`, `FUND_CCY`, `EFRONT`, `NAV_BACKDATED` |
| `NAV` | `NAV_FUND_NO`, `NAV_DATE_NAV`, `NAV_QT_TOT_PART`, `NAV_PUB` (`'A'` = published), `NAV_CONTROLE` (`'Y'` = controlled) |

**Notes on the data model.** A *lot* belongs to one fund and one NAV date (`D_NAV`); a NAV date can have several lots. The ledger of a NAV is the set of entries whose lot falls in a **lot window `(LOT_FROM, LOT_TO]`**: lower bound excluded, upper bound included. The window queries compute that window.

## 5. Queries

### Q00 â€” Fund sheet

**When:** always, first.
**Inputs:** `{{FUND}}`.
**Output:** 0 or 1 row: `FA_NUM`, `F_NAME`, `F_CCY`, `EFRONT`, `NAV_BACKDATED`.
**Rules:** no row â†’ fund unknown. `EFRONT = '1'` â†’ refuse (decision of the Head of Fund Accounting, 01/10/2026; stricter than LUXIS, which also looks at `EFRONT_DATE`; `2` is the default "no"). `NAV_BACKDATED` = 1 for any value other than `2` (LUXIS `DECODE(NVL(NAV_BACKDATED,2),2,0,1)`).

```sql
SELECT t.FA_NUM, MIN(t.FUND_NAME) AS F_NAME, MIN(t.FUND_CCY) AS F_CCY,
       MAX(CAST(t.EFRONT AS VARCHAR)) AS EFRONT,
       CASE WHEN COALESCE(MAX(CAST(t.NAV_BACKDATED AS INTEGER)), 2) <> 2 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS NAV_BACKDATED
FROM {{TBL_TFM}} t
WHERE t.FA_NUM = {{FUND}}
GROUP BY t.FA_NUM
```

### Q01 â€” Calculation date â†’ NAV date

**When:** IRP single-NAV mode with `calc_date` (no `nav_date`).
**Inputs:** `{{FUND}}`, `{{CALC}}` (= `calc_date`).
**Output:** 1 row, `NAV_DATE` (null if none) â†’ null is an error.
**Rule (`GET_NAV_DATE_CALCUL`):** the calculation date of a NAV is the processing day (`TRUNC(D_H_PROCESS)`) of its last lot; take the latest NAV whose calculation date is â‰¤ `{{CALC}}`.

```sql
WITH last_lot AS (
  SELECT l.D_NAV, l.N_LOT, l.D_H_PROCESS, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY l.D_NAV ORDER BY l.N_LOT DESC) AS RN
  FROM {{TBL_AMS_LOT}} l
  WHERE l.C_FUND = {{FUND}} AND l.D_NAV <= {{CALC}}),
nav_calc AS (
  SELECT D_NAV, N_LOT, CAST(D_H_PROCESS AS DATE) AS D_CALC FROM last_lot WHERE RN = 1)
SELECT MAX(D_NAV) AS NAV_DATE FROM nav_calc WHERE D_CALC <= CAST({{CALC}} AS DATE)
```

### Q02 â€” Last annual closing before the NAV

**When:** IRP single-NAV mode, `period` âˆˆ {13, 14, 16}.
**Inputs:** `{{FUND}}`, `{{NAV}}`, `{{SEUIL_RESULTAT}}` (40000).
**Output:** 0 or 1 row: `LOT_RS` (lot of the closing entry), `LOT_CLOT` (last lot before it), `DATE_NAV_CLOT` (NAV of that lot = "closing NAV").
**Rules (`GET_DATE_NAV_LAST_CLOSING`):** a closing entry is a service `RS` entry, account â‰¥ threshold except 47410, 57410, 999998, `R_EXCHANGE <> 0`, status 20, in the last lot of its accounting day and account, and not reversed (a status-30 entry on the same account and entry number). The closing lot is the last lot of the fund strictly before the `RS` lot; its NAV must be strictly before `{{NAV}}`. Latest `LOT_RS` wins. No row = no closing before this NAV (not an error).
**Performance rule:** the fund's lot list must stay a semi-join on a sub-query, **never** a literal `IN (â€¦)` list or a `VALUES` join (Dremio silently truncates those).

```sql
WITH t AS (
  SELECT c.N_LOT, c.N_ENTRY, c.D_ACC, c.C_N_ACC, c.C_SRV, c.R_EXCHANGE, c.C_STATUS
  FROM {{TBL_AMS_CASH_MVT}} c
  WHERE c.C_FUND = {{FUND}} AND c.C_SRV = 'RS'
    AND c.N_LOT IN (SELECT l.N_LOT FROM {{TBL_AMS_LOT}} l WHERE l.C_FUND = {{FUND}} AND l.D_NAV <= {{NAV}})),
rs AS (
  SELECT t.* FROM t
  WHERE t.C_N_ACC >= {{SEUIL_RESULTAT}} AND t.C_N_ACC NOT IN (47410, 57410, 999998) AND t.R_EXCHANGE <> 0 AND t.C_STATUS = 20),
maxlot AS (SELECT t.D_ACC, t.C_N_ACC, MAX(t.N_LOT) AS ML FROM t GROUP BY t.D_ACC, t.C_N_ACC),
rev AS (SELECT DISTINCT t.C_N_ACC, t.N_ENTRY FROM t WHERE t.C_STATUS = 30),
cand AS (
  SELECT rs.N_LOT, rs.D_ACC FROM rs
  JOIN maxlot m ON m.D_ACC = rs.D_ACC AND m.C_N_ACC = rs.C_N_ACC AND m.ML = rs.N_LOT
  LEFT JOIN rev r ON r.C_N_ACC = rs.C_N_ACC AND r.N_ENTRY = rs.N_ENTRY
  WHERE r.N_ENTRY IS NULL),
lots AS (SELECT l.N_LOT, l.D_NAV FROM {{TBL_AMS_LOT}} l WHERE l.C_FUND = {{FUND}}),
clot AS (SELECT c.N_LOT AS LOT_RS, MAX(l.N_LOT) AS LOT_CLOT FROM cand c JOIN lots l ON l.N_LOT < c.N_LOT GROUP BY c.N_LOT)
SELECT k.LOT_RS, k.LOT_CLOT, l.D_NAV AS DATE_NAV_CLOT
FROM clot k JOIN lots l ON l.N_LOT = k.LOT_CLOT
WHERE l.D_NAV < {{NAV}}
ORDER BY k.LOT_RS DESC
LIMIT 1
```

### Window queries â€” common contract

All window queries (Q10â€“Q16, Q18) return **0 or 1 row** with the same six columns:

| Column | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `NAV_TO` | NAV date at the end of the window (included) |
| `NAV_FROM` | NAV date at the start of the window (excluded); may be null |
| `LOT_FROM` | exclusive lower lot bound. Last lot of `NAV_FROM`; **smallest** lot of `NAV_FROM` if the fund is backdated; `0` if `NAV_FROM` is null / has no lot |
| `LOT_TO` | inclusive upper lot bound: last lot of `NAV_TO` |
| `TRADE_DATE_MAX` | `NAV_TO` if the fund is backdated (`NAV_BACKDATED = 1`), else null. Q20 then drops entries with `D_TRADE > TRADE_DATE_MAX` |
| `LOT_RESULT_FROM` | only meaningful for period 16, null otherwise |

Common CTEs in every window query:

- `cal`: calendar of the fund â€” one row per NAV date (`D_NAV`) with `MIN(N_LOT)` and `MAX(N_LOT)`, bounded by the end date (**NAVs are read from the lots table, not from the LUXIS NAV table**, except where stated).
- `fonds`: the backdated flag of the fund, read from `{{TBL_TFM}}` (same rule as Q00).

### Q10 â€” Window, period 1 ("since previous NAV")

**When:** IRP single NAV, `period = 1`. **Inputs:** `{{FUND}}`, `{{NAV}}`. **No row** if the fund has no lot on `{{NAV}}`.

```sql
WITH cal AS (
  SELECT l.D_NAV, MIN(l.N_LOT) AS LOT_MIN, MAX(l.N_LOT) AS LOT_MAX
  FROM {{TBL_AMS_LOT}} l
  WHERE l.C_FUND = {{FUND}} AND l.D_NAV <= {{NAV}}
  GROUP BY l.D_NAV),
fonds AS (
  SELECT CASE WHEN COALESCE(MAX(CAST(t.NAV_BACKDATED AS INTEGER)), 2) <> 2 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS BACKDATED
  FROM {{TBL_TFM}} t WHERE t.FA_NUM = {{FUND}}),
debut AS (
  SELECT MAX(c.D_NAV) AS NAV_FROM FROM cal c WHERE c.D_NAV < {{NAV}})
SELECT a.D_NAV AS NAV_TO, d.NAV_FROM AS NAV_FROM,
       COALESCE(CASE WHEN f.BACKDATED = 1 THEN b.LOT_MIN ELSE b.LOT_MAX END, 0) AS LOT_FROM,
       a.LOT_MAX AS LOT_TO,
       CASE WHEN f.BACKDATED = 1 THEN a.D_NAV END AS TRADE_DATE_MAX,
       CAST(NULL AS BIGINT) AS LOT_RESULT_FROM
FROM cal a
CROSS JOIN debut d
CROSS JOIN fonds f
LEFT JOIN cal b ON b.D_NAV = d.NAV_FROM
WHERE a.D_NAV = {{NAV}}
```

### Q11 â€” Window, period 2 ("one week")

**When:** IRP single NAV, `period = 2`. Identical to Q10 except the start NAV is the last NAV â‰¤ `{{NAV}}` âˆ’ 7 days.

```sql
WITH cal AS (
  SELECT l.D_NAV, MIN(l.N_LOT) AS LOT_MIN, MAX(l.N_LOT) AS LOT_MAX
  FROM {{TBL_AMS_LOT}} l
  WHERE l.C_FUND = {{FUND}} AND l.D_NAV <= {{NAV}}
  GROUP BY l.D_NAV),
fonds AS (
  SELECT CASE WHEN COALESCE(MAX(CAST(t.NAV_BACKDATED AS INTEGER)), 2) <> 2 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS BACKDATED
  FROM {{TBL_TFM}} t WHERE t.FA_NUM = {{FUND}}),
debut AS (
  SELECT MAX(c.D_NAV) AS NAV_FROM FROM cal c WHERE c.D_NAV <= {{NAV}} - INTERVAL '7' DAY)
SELECT a.D_NAV AS NAV_TO, d.NAV_FROM AS NAV_FROM,
       COALESCE(CASE WHEN f.BACKDATED = 1 THEN b.LOT_MIN ELSE b.LOT_MAX END, 0) AS LOT_FROM,
       a.LOT_MAX AS LOT_TO,
       CASE WHEN f.BACKDATED = 1 THEN a.D_NAV END AS TRADE_DATE_MAX,
       CAST(NULL AS BIGINT) AS LOT_RESULT_FROM
FROM cal a
CROSS JOIN debut d
CROSS JOIN fonds f
LEFT JOIN cal b ON b.D_NAV = d.NAV_FROM
WHERE a.D_NAV = {{NAV}}
```

### Q12 â€” Window, period 13 ("begin of accounting year")

**When:** IRP single NAV, `period = 13`. **Inputs:** `{{FUND}}`, `{{NAV}}`, `{{CLOSING_NAV}}` + flag `HAS_CLOSING` when Q02 returned a row.
**Rule (corrected, fixed):** with a closing, the start NAV is the **closing NAV itself** (last NAV â‰¤ `{{CLOSING_NAV}}`), so the first NAV after the closing is kept and the result equals period 14. (The original LUXIS rule starts after the closing and drops that NAV; it is not used.) Without a closing, the start NAV is the fund's first NAV with shares in the LUXIS NAV table (`NAV_QT_TOT_PART <> 0`) and that NAV's entries are excluded; with no such NAV, `LOT_FROM = 0`.

```sql
WITH cal AS (
  SELECT l.D_NAV, MIN(l.N_LOT) AS LOT_MIN, MAX(l.N_LOT) AS LOT_MAX
  FROM {{TBL_AMS_LOT}} l
  WHERE l.C_FUND = {{FUND}} AND l.D_NAV <= {{NAV}}
  GROUP BY l.D_NAV),
fonds AS (
  SELECT CASE WHEN COALESCE(MAX(CAST(t.NAV_BACKDATED AS INTEGER)), 2) <> 2 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS BACKDATED
  FROM {{TBL_TFM}} t WHERE t.FA_NUM = {{FUND}}),
debut AS (
--#IF HAS_CLOSING
  SELECT MAX(c.D_NAV) AS NAV_FROM FROM cal c WHERE c.D_NAV <= {{CLOSING_NAV}}
--#ELSE
  SELECT MIN(n.NAV_DATE_NAV) AS NAV_FROM FROM {{TBL_NAV}} n WHERE n.NAV_FUND_NO = {{FUND}} AND n.NAV_QT_TOT_PART <> 0
--#END
  )
SELECT a.D_NAV AS NAV_TO, d.NAV_FROM AS NAV_FROM,
       COALESCE(CASE WHEN f.BACKDATED = 1 THEN b.LOT_MIN ELSE b.LOT_MAX END, 0) AS LOT_FROM,
       a.LOT_MAX AS LOT_TO,
       CASE WHEN f.BACKDATED = 1 THEN a.D_NAV END AS TRADE_DATE_MAX,
       CAST(NULL AS BIGINT) AS LOT_RESULT_FROM
FROM cal a
CROSS JOIN debut d
CROSS JOIN fonds f
LEFT JOIN cal b ON b.D_NAV = d.NAV_FROM
WHERE a.D_NAV = {{NAV}}
```

### Q13 â€” Window, period 14 ("since last accounting year")

**When:** IRP single NAV, `period = 14`. Same inputs and flag as Q12. Start NAV = the **closing NAV itself** (the first NAV after the closing is kept). Without a closing: first NAV with shares, as in Q12.

```sql
WITH cal AS (
  SELECT l.D_NAV, MIN(l.N_LOT) AS LOT_MIN, MAX(l.N_LOT) AS LOT_MAX
  FROM {{TBL_AMS_LOT}} l
  WHERE l.C_FUND = {{FUND}} AND l.D_NAV <= {{NAV}}
  GROUP BY l.D_NAV),
fonds AS (
  SELECT CASE WHEN COALESCE(MAX(CAST(t.NAV_BACKDATED AS INTEGER)), 2) <> 2 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS BACKDATED
  FROM {{TBL_TFM}} t WHERE t.FA_NUM = {{FUND}}),
debut AS (
--#IF HAS_CLOSING
  SELECT MAX(c.D_NAV) AS NAV_FROM FROM cal c WHERE c.D_NAV <= {{CLOSING_NAV}}
--#ELSE
  SELECT MIN(n.NAV_DATE_NAV) AS NAV_FROM FROM {{TBL_NAV}} n WHERE n.NAV_FUND_NO = {{FUND}} AND n.NAV_QT_TOT_PART <> 0
--#END
  )
SELECT a.D_NAV AS NAV_TO, d.NAV_FROM AS NAV_FROM,
       COALESCE(CASE WHEN f.BACKDATED = 1 THEN b.LOT_MIN ELSE b.LOT_MAX END, 0) AS LOT_FROM,
       a.LOT_MAX AS LOT_TO,
       CASE WHEN f.BACKDATED = 1 THEN a.D_NAV END AS TRADE_DATE_MAX,
       CAST(NULL AS BIGINT) AS LOT_RESULT_FROM
FROM cal a
CROSS JOIN debut d
CROSS JOIN fonds f
LEFT JOIN cal b ON b.D_NAV = d.NAV_FROM
WHERE a.D_NAV = {{NAV}}
```

### Q14 â€” Window, period 16 ("financial statement consolidation")

**When:** IRP single NAV, `period = 16`. Same inputs and flag as Q12.
**Rule (corrected, fixed):** this query is still run, but only `LOT_TO` (and `NAV_FROM` = closing NAV) are used. `LOT_FROM` is always `0` and `LOT_RESULT_FROM` is **ignored when a closing exists**: Q20 splits balance accounts (< `SEUIL_RESULTAT`, every lot up to `LOT_TO`) from result accounts (â‰¥ threshold, only lots after the closing lot **and** accounting date after the closing NAV) with the closing from Q02 (flag `P16_CORRIGE`). Without a closing, Q20 falls back to `P16_LUXIS` with `LOT_RESULT_FROM = 0`, i.e. all lots for every account.

```sql
WITH cal AS (
  SELECT l.D_NAV, MIN(l.N_LOT) AS LOT_MIN, MAX(l.N_LOT) AS LOT_MAX
  FROM {{TBL_AMS_LOT}} l
  WHERE l.C_FUND = {{FUND}} AND l.D_NAV <= {{NAV}}
  GROUP BY l.D_NAV),
fonds AS (
  SELECT CASE WHEN COALESCE(MAX(CAST(t.NAV_BACKDATED AS INTEGER)), 2) <> 2 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS BACKDATED
  FROM {{TBL_TFM}} t WHERE t.FA_NUM = {{FUND}}),
apres AS (
--#IF HAS_CLOSING
  SELECT MIN(c.D_NAV) AS NAV_FIRST FROM cal c WHERE c.D_NAV > {{CLOSING_NAV}} AND c.D_NAV <= {{NAV}})
--#ELSE
  SELECT MIN(n.NAV_DATE_NAV) AS NAV_FIRST FROM {{TBL_NAV}} n WHERE n.NAV_FUND_NO = {{FUND}} AND n.NAV_QT_TOT_PART <> 0)
--#END
SELECT a.D_NAV AS NAV_TO,
--#IF HAS_CLOSING
       {{CLOSING_NAV}} AS NAV_FROM,
--#ELSE
       CAST(NULL AS TIMESTAMP) AS NAV_FROM,
--#END
       0 AS LOT_FROM, a.LOT_MAX AS LOT_TO,
       CASE WHEN f.BACKDATED = 1 THEN a.D_NAV END AS TRADE_DATE_MAX,
--#IF HAS_CLOSING
       COALESCE(CASE WHEN f.BACKDATED = 1 THEN r.LOT_MIN ELSE r.LOT_MAX END, a.LOT_MAX) AS LOT_RESULT_FROM
--#ELSE
       COALESCE(CASE WHEN f.BACKDATED = 1 THEN r.LOT_MIN ELSE r.LOT_MAX END, 0) AS LOT_RESULT_FROM
--#END
FROM cal a
CROSS JOIN apres p
CROSS JOIN fonds f
LEFT JOIN cal r ON r.D_NAV = p.NAV_FIRST
WHERE a.D_NAV = {{NAV}}
```

### Q16 â€” Window, calendar periods (codes 3â€“12 and 15)

**When:** IRP single NAV, `period` âˆˆ {3â€¦12, 15}. **Inputs:** `{{FUND}}`, `{{NAV}}`, and **one** flag among `C03`â€¦`C12`, `C15` (the one matching the period).
**Rule:** start NAV = last NAV of the fund on or before a target date `D_FROM` (table below); code 15 starts from the first NAV with shares (LUXIS NAV table), whose entries are therefore excluded; if there is none, `LOT_FROM = 0`.

| Flag | `D_FROM` expression |
|---|---|
| `C03` | `{{NAV}} - INTERVAL '14' DAY` |
| `C04`â€¦`C08` | `{{NAV}}` minus *M* months, *M* = 1, 2, 3, 6, 12 for codes 4, 5, 6, 7, 8. Oracle `ADD_MONTHS` rule: if `{{NAV}}` is the last day of its month the result is the last day of the target month, otherwise the same day (clamped to the target month's last day, e.g. 30/03 âˆ’ 1 month = 28/02) |
| `C09` | `CAST(DATE_TRUNC('MONTH', {{NAV}}) AS TIMESTAMP) - INTERVAL '1' DAY` |
| `C10` | `CAST(DATE_TRUNC('QUARTER', {{NAV}}) AS TIMESTAMP) - INTERVAL '1' DAY` |
| `C11` | month(`{{NAV}}`) < 7 â†’ `CAST(DATE_TRUNC('YEAR', {{NAV}}) AS TIMESTAMP) - INTERVAL '1' DAY`; otherwise `TIMESTAMPADD(MONTH, 6, CAST(DATE_TRUNC('YEAR', {{NAV}}) AS TIMESTAMP)) - INTERVAL '1' DAY` |
| `C12` | `CAST(DATE_TRUNC('YEAR', {{NAV}}) AS TIMESTAMP) - INTERVAL '1' DAY` |

```sql
WITH cal AS (
  SELECT l.D_NAV, MIN(l.N_LOT) AS LOT_MIN, MAX(l.N_LOT) AS LOT_MAX
  FROM {{TBL_AMS_LOT}} l
  WHERE l.C_FUND = {{FUND}} AND l.D_NAV <= {{NAV}}
  GROUP BY l.D_NAV),
fonds AS (
  SELECT CASE WHEN COALESCE(MAX(CAST(t.NAV_BACKDATED AS INTEGER)), 2) <> 2 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS BACKDATED
  FROM {{TBL_TFM}} t WHERE t.FA_NUM = {{FUND}}),
--#IF C15
debut AS (
  SELECT MIN(n.NAV_DATE_NAV) AS NAV_FROM FROM {{TBL_NAV}} n WHERE n.NAV_FUND_NO = {{FUND}} AND n.NAV_QT_TOT_PART <> 0)
--#ELSE
cible AS (
  SELECT <D_FROM expression of the raised flag, see table> AS D_FROM
  ),
debut AS (
  SELECT MAX(c.D_NAV) AS NAV_FROM FROM cal c CROSS JOIN cible t WHERE c.D_NAV <= t.D_FROM)
--#END
SELECT a.D_NAV AS NAV_TO, d.NAV_FROM AS NAV_FROM,
       COALESCE(CASE WHEN f.BACKDATED = 1 THEN b.LOT_MIN ELSE b.LOT_MAX END, 0) AS LOT_FROM,
       a.LOT_MAX AS LOT_TO,
       CASE WHEN f.BACKDATED = 1 THEN a.D_NAV END AS TRADE_DATE_MAX,
       CAST(NULL AS BIGINT) AS LOT_RESULT_FROM
FROM cal a
CROSS JOIN debut d
CROSS JOIN fonds f
LEFT JOIN cal b ON b.D_NAV = d.NAV_FROM
WHERE a.D_NAV = {{NAV}}
```

Worked `D_FROM` expression for `C04`â€“`C08` (substitute *M*):

```sql
CASE WHEN CAST({{NAV}} AS DATE) = LAST_DAY(CAST({{NAV}} AS DATE))
     THEN CAST(LAST_DAY(TIMESTAMPADD(MONTH, -M, {{NAV}})) AS TIMESTAMP)
     ELSE TIMESTAMPADD(MONTH, -M, {{NAV}}) END
```

### Q15 â€” Window, date range (IRP range mode and BCR `plage`)

**When:** IRP with `date_from` + `date_to`, or BCR with `bcr_period = plage`. **Inputs:** `{{FUND}}`, `{{DATE_FROM}}`, `{{DATE_TO}}`.
**Rule (`proc_Bcr_Grands_Livres`), with one assumed deviation:** `NAV_TO` = last NAV on or before `date_to`. `proc_Bcr_Grands_Livres` itself takes `NAV_FROM` = last NAV on or before `date_from` (excluded from the window), but this app takes `NAV_FROM` = last NAV strictly before `date_from`, so `date_from`'s own NAV, when one exists, is included rather than excluded (decision Oscar MISCHLER, 12/10/2026, see `sql\15_fenetre_bcr.sql` header). **No row** if the fund has no NAV on or before `date_to` (error).

```sql
WITH cal AS (
  SELECT l.D_NAV, MIN(l.N_LOT) AS LOT_MIN, MAX(l.N_LOT) AS LOT_MAX
  FROM {{TBL_AMS_LOT}} l
  WHERE l.C_FUND = {{FUND}} AND l.D_NAV <= {{DATE_TO}}
  GROUP BY l.D_NAV),
fonds AS (
  SELECT CASE WHEN COALESCE(MAX(CAST(t.NAV_BACKDATED AS INTEGER)), 2) <> 2 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS BACKDATED
  FROM {{TBL_TFM}} t WHERE t.FA_NUM = {{FUND}}),
debut AS (SELECT MAX(c.D_NAV) AS NAV_FROM FROM cal c WHERE c.D_NAV < {{DATE_FROM}}),
fin AS (SELECT MAX(c.D_NAV) AS NAV_TO FROM cal c)
SELECT a.D_NAV AS NAV_TO, d.NAV_FROM AS NAV_FROM,
       COALESCE(CASE WHEN f.BACKDATED = 1 THEN b.LOT_MIN ELSE b.LOT_MAX END, 0) AS LOT_FROM,
       a.LOT_MAX AS LOT_TO,
       CASE WHEN f.BACKDATED = 1 THEN a.D_NAV END AS TRADE_DATE_MAX,
       CAST(NULL AS BIGINT) AS LOT_RESULT_FROM
FROM cal a
CROSS JOIN fin z
CROSS JOIN debut d
CROSS JOIN fonds f
LEFT JOIN cal b ON b.D_NAV = d.NAV_FROM
WHERE a.D_NAV = z.NAV_TO
```

### Q18 â€” Window, BCR from the LUXIS NAV table

**When:** BCR with `bcr_period` âˆˆ {`last_available_day`, `to_last_date_nav`}. **Inputs:** `{{FUND}}`, `{{TODAY}}` (execution date), and `{{DATE_FROM}}` + flag `BCR_NAV_PUBLIEE` for `to_last_date_nav` only.
**Rules (`PKG_LUXREP_QUERIES`):**

| Mode | `NAV_TO` | `NAV_FROM` |
|---|---|---|
| `last_available_day` (flag absent) | latest NAV â‰¤ `TODAY` with `NAV_CONTROLE = 'Y'` | latest controlled NAV strictly before `NAV_TO`. The requested dates are ignored |
| `to_last_date_nav` (flag raised) | latest NAV â‰¤ `TODAY` with `NAV_PUB = 'A'` | earliest published NAV â‰¥ `LEAST(DATE_FROM, NAV_TO)` |

`LOT_FROM` / `LOT_TO` come from `GET_LOT_DATE_NAV(â€¦, 0)`: the largest lot of that **exact** NAV date, or **0** if that date has no lot (a NAV date without lot empties the window `LOT_TO = 0` or opens it from the origin `LOT_FROM = 0`). **No row** if either NAV date is missing (LUXIS would silently substitute SYSDATE; this specification instead raises an error).

```sql
WITH nav AS (
  SELECT n.NAV_DATE_NAV AS D_NAV
  FROM {{TBL_NAV}} n
  WHERE n.NAV_FUND_NO = {{FUND}}
--#IF BCR_NAV_PUBLIEE
    AND n.NAV_PUB = 'A'),
--#ELSE
    AND n.NAV_CONTROLE = 'Y'),
--#END
fin AS (SELECT MAX(x.D_NAV) AS NAV_TO FROM nav x WHERE x.D_NAV <= {{TODAY}}),
debut AS (
--#IF BCR_NAV_PUBLIEE
  SELECT MIN(x.D_NAV) AS NAV_FROM FROM nav x CROSS JOIN fin z
  WHERE x.D_NAV >= CASE WHEN {{DATE_FROM}} < z.NAV_TO THEN {{DATE_FROM}} ELSE z.NAV_TO END),
--#ELSE
  SELECT MAX(x.D_NAV) AS NAV_FROM FROM nav x CROSS JOIN fin z WHERE x.D_NAV < z.NAV_TO),
--#END
cal AS (
  SELECT l.D_NAV, MIN(l.N_LOT) AS LOT_MIN, MAX(l.N_LOT) AS LOT_MAX
  FROM {{TBL_AMS_LOT}} l
  WHERE l.C_FUND = {{FUND}}
  GROUP BY l.D_NAV),
fonds AS (
  SELECT CASE WHEN COALESCE(MAX(CAST(t.NAV_BACKDATED AS INTEGER)), 2) <> 2 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS BACKDATED
  FROM {{TBL_TFM}} t WHERE t.FA_NUM = {{FUND}})
SELECT z.NAV_TO AS NAV_TO, d.NAV_FROM AS NAV_FROM,
       COALESCE(CASE WHEN f.BACKDATED = 1 THEN b.LOT_MIN ELSE b.LOT_MAX END, 0) AS LOT_FROM,
       COALESCE(a.LOT_MAX, 0) AS LOT_TO,
       CASE WHEN f.BACKDATED = 1 THEN z.NAV_TO END AS TRADE_DATE_MAX,
       CAST(NULL AS BIGINT) AS LOT_RESULT_FROM
FROM fin z
CROSS JOIN debut d
CROSS JOIN fonds f
LEFT JOIN cal a ON a.D_NAV = z.NAV_TO
LEFT JOIN cal b ON b.D_NAV = d.NAV_FROM
WHERE z.NAV_TO IS NOT NULL AND d.NAV_FROM IS NOT NULL
```

### Q20 â€” Ledger entries (the report itself)

**When:** always, once the window is known. **This is the only query whose rows go into the output file.**
**Inputs and flags:** see 4.3.
**Output:** one row per ledger entry, in the final order. The 23 columns `SUBFUND_NUMBER â€¦ STATUS` feed the IRP file; the BCR file uses a subset (section 7). Four technical columns follow (`N_LOT`, `N_LINE`, `PTF_MANAGER`, `FONDS_ORIGINE`) and are used only by the controls, not written to the file.

**Rules**

- **Population:** entries of the fund with `N_LOT > LOT_FROM AND N_LOT <= LOT_TO`, restricted to lots that exist for the fund in that window (semi-join).
- **Account range:** IRP optional; BCR `acc_from`â€“`acc_to` (default 1450â€“999999).
- **Backdated fund:** `D_TRADE <= TRADE_MAX`.
- **Period 16:** account < threshold â†’ every lot up to `LOT_TO`; account â‰¥ threshold â†’ with a closing (`P16_CORRIGE`) lots after `CLOSING_LOT` and accounting date after `CLOSING_NAV`; without a closing (`P16_LUXIS`, `LOT_RESULT_FROM = 0`) every lot.
- **Previous balance:** `A_BALANCE âˆ’ A_MVT` if the way is `CR`, else `A_BALANCE + A_MVT`.
- **Account name:** `L_NAME` of the latest version (highest `N_LOT`) of the account in the chart of accounts. IRP: the chart of the fund's latest lot (`AMS_PORTFOLIO`). BCR: the **fixed chart `'20'`** (LuxRep hard-codes it).
- **Fund name and currency:** scalar sub-queries on Table Fonds, one per fund number. Keep them as scalar sub-queries â€” a join or cross join with Table Fonds turns a 7 s query into more than 200 s for 20 000 lines.
- **Order** (deduced from LUXIS output, proven on 242013 and 280287): numeric keys cast to `DOUBLE`, an empty key counts as 0. A final tie-break makes repeated runs identical; it never changes which lines are returned.
  - IRP: account, rubric, account currency, accounting date, `Entry Next`, lot, line
  - BCR: account, sub-account, account currency, accounting date, `Entry`, `Entry Ptf`, lot, line
- Do **not** sort, name or compute anything outside this query.

```sql
--#IF PLAN_FIXE
WITH noms AS (
  SELECT x.C_N_ACC, x.L_NAME FROM (
    SELECT d.C_N_ACC, d.L_NAME, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY d.C_N_ACC ORDER BY d.N_LOT DESC) AS RN
    FROM {{TBL_AMS_ACC_DEF}} d WHERE d.C_ACC_PLAN = {{PLAN}}) x
  WHERE x.RN = 1)
--#ELSE
WITH plan AS (
  SELECT p.C_ACC_PLAN FROM {{TBL_AMS_PORTFOLIO}} p WHERE p.C_FUND = {{FUND}} ORDER BY p.N_LOT DESC LIMIT 1),
noms AS (
  SELECT x.C_N_ACC, x.L_NAME FROM (
    SELECT d.C_N_ACC, d.L_NAME, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY d.C_N_ACC ORDER BY d.N_LOT DESC) AS RN
    FROM {{TBL_AMS_ACC_DEF}} d JOIN plan pl ON d.C_ACC_PLAN = pl.C_ACC_PLAN) x
  WHERE x.RN = 1)
--#END
SELECT c.C_FUND AS SUBFUND_NUMBER,
       (SELECT MIN(t.FUND_NAME) FROM {{TBL_TFM}} t WHERE t.FA_NUM = {{FUND}}) AS SUBFUND_NAME,
       (SELECT MIN(t.FUND_CCY) FROM {{TBL_TFM}} t WHERE t.FA_NUM = {{FUND}}) AS SUBFUND_CCY,
       c.C_N_ACC AS ACCOUNT_NUMBER, c.N_SUF AS ACCOUNT_RUBRIC, n.L_NAME AS ACCOUNT_NAME,
       c.C_CCY AS ACCOUNT_CCY, c.C_ACC_WAY AS DEBIT_CREDIT, c.C_SRV AS CODE_SERVICE, c.C_OPE AS OPERATION_CODE,
       c.D_ACC AS ACCOUNTING_DATE, c.D_TRADE AS TRADE_DATE, c.D_VALUE AS VALUE_DATE, c.D_MATURITY AS MATURITY_DATE,
       c.L_MVT AS DESCRIPTION, c.N_ENTRY AS ENTRY, c.N_ENTRY_PTF AS ENTRY_PTF, c."N_NEXT" AS ENTRY_NEXT,
       c.A_MVT AS AMOUNT_ACCOUNT_CCY, c.A_MVT_PTF AS AMOUNT_SUBFUND_CCY,
       CASE WHEN c.C_ACC_WAY = 'CR' THEN c.A_BALANCE - c.A_MVT ELSE c.A_BALANCE + c.A_MVT END AS PREVIOUS_BALANCE_ACCOUNT_CCY,
       c.A_BALANCE AS BALANCE_ACCOUNT_CCY, c.C_STATUS AS STATUS,
       c.N_LOT, c.N_LINE, c.C_N_PTF_MANAGER AS PTF_MANAGER, c.C_FUND AS FONDS_ORIGINE
FROM {{TBL_AMS_CASH_MVT}} c
LEFT JOIN noms n ON n.C_N_ACC = c.C_N_ACC
WHERE c.C_FUND = {{FUND}} AND c.N_LOT > {{LOT_FROM}} AND c.N_LOT <= {{LOT_TO}}
  AND c.N_LOT IN (SELECT l.N_LOT FROM {{TBL_AMS_LOT}} l WHERE l.C_FUND = {{FUND}} AND l.N_LOT > {{LOT_FROM}} AND l.N_LOT <= {{LOT_TO}})
--#IF COMPTE_DE
  AND c.C_N_ACC >= {{ACC_FROM}}
--#END
--#IF COMPTE_A
  AND c.C_N_ACC <= {{ACC_TO}}
--#END
--#IF TRADE_MAX
  AND c.D_TRADE <= {{TRADE_MAX}}
--#END
--#IF P16_LUXIS
  AND (c.C_N_ACC < {{SEUIL_RESULTAT}} OR c.N_LOT > {{LOT_RESULT_FROM}})
--#END
--#IF P16_CORRIGE
  AND (c.C_N_ACC < {{SEUIL_RESULTAT}} OR (c.N_LOT > {{CLOSING_LOT}} AND c.D_ACC > {{CLOSING_NAV}}))
--#END
--#IF TRI_IRP
ORDER BY COALESCE(CAST(c.C_N_ACC AS DOUBLE), 0), COALESCE(CAST(c.N_SUF AS DOUBLE), 0), c.C_CCY, CAST(c.D_ACC AS DATE),
         COALESCE(CAST(c."N_NEXT" AS DOUBLE), 0), COALESCE(CAST(c.N_LOT AS DOUBLE), 0), COALESCE(CAST(c.N_LINE AS DOUBLE), 0),
         COALESCE(CAST(c.A_MVT AS DOUBLE), 0), c.C_ACC_WAY
--#END
--#IF TRI_BCR
ORDER BY COALESCE(CAST(c.C_N_ACC AS DOUBLE), 0), COALESCE(CAST(c.N_SUF AS DOUBLE), 0), c.C_CCY, CAST(c.D_ACC AS DATE),
         COALESCE(CAST(c.N_ENTRY AS DOUBLE), 0), COALESCE(CAST(c.N_ENTRY_PTF AS DOUBLE), 0),
         COALESCE(CAST(c.N_LOT AS DOUBLE), 0), COALESCE(CAST(c.N_LINE AS DOUBLE), 0),
         COALESCE(CAST(c.A_MVT AS DOUBLE), 0), COALESCE(CAST(c."N_NEXT" AS DOUBLE), 0), c.C_ACC_WAY
--#END
```

### Q35 â€” Final balances (control query)

**When:** after Q20, only if it returned at least one row.
**Inputs:** `{{FUND}}`, `{{LOT_TO}}` (= `window.LOT_TO`).
**Output:** one row per position of the fund at the last lot of the window. A position is (account, rubric, account currency, maturity date, portfolio manager).
`BALANCE_MIN` and `BALANCE_MAX` are both returned to prove that the several rows of one position (`Y_VARIATION` = Y and N) carry the same balance.
Not written to the report; used by control C4 (6.2).

```sql
SELECT p.C_N_ACC AS ACCOUNT_NUMBER, p.N_SUF AS ACCOUNT_RUBRIC, p.C_ACC_CCY AS ACCOUNT_CCY, p.D_MATURITY AS MATURITY_DATE,
       p.C_N_PTF_MANAGER AS PTF_MANAGER, MIN(p.A_BALANCE) AS BALANCE_MIN, MAX(p.A_BALANCE) AS BALANCE_MAX, COUNT(*) AS N_LIGNES
FROM {{TBL_AMS_ACC_POS}} p
WHERE p.C_FUND = {{FUND}} AND p.N_LOT = {{LOT_TO}}
GROUP BY p.C_N_ACC, p.N_SUF, p.C_ACC_CCY, p.D_MATURITY, p.C_N_PTF_MANAGER
```

### Q51 â€” Latest available NAV (history note, optional)

**When:** only if the start of the requested period (`nav`, `NAV_FROM` or `date_from`, whichever is earliest) is older than *today âˆ’ 3 years*; otherwise the answer is known in advance. It is **never a refusal**, only a note: the Reporting team wants three years of history, and a request starting before *(latest NAV in the lots table) âˆ’ 3 years* gets a "beyond 3 years of history" warning.
**Output:** one row, `DERNIERE_NAV`.

```sql
SELECT MAX(l.D_NAV) AS DERNIERE_NAV
FROM {{TBL_AMS_LOT}} l
```

## 6. Query summary and controls

### 6.1 Which queries run for which request

| Request | Queries, in order |
|---|---|
| IRP, `nav_date`, period 1 / 2 | Q00 â†’ Q10 / Q11 â†’ Q20 â†’ Q35 |
| IRP, `calc_date`, period 1 / 2 | Q00 â†’ Q01 â†’ Q10 / Q11 â†’ Q20 â†’ Q35 |
| IRP, period 13 / 14 / 16 | Q00 â†’ (Q01) â†’ Q02 â†’ Q12 / Q13 / Q14 â†’ Q20 â†’ Q35 |
| IRP, period 3â€“12, 15 | Q00 â†’ (Q01) â†’ Q16 â†’ Q20 â†’ Q35 |
| IRP, range | Q00 â†’ Q15 â†’ Q20 â†’ Q35 |
| BCR `plage` | Q00 â†’ Q15 â†’ Q20 â†’ Q35 |
| BCR `last_available_day` / `to_last_date_nav` | Q00 â†’ Q18 â†’ Q20 â†’ Q35 |

(Q51 may be added at the end of any of them.)

### 6.2 Controls computed on the result (not part of the file)

| # | Control | Rule | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|
| C1 | Credit / debit balance | Î£ `AMOUNT_SUBFUND_CCY` where `DEBIT_CREDIT='CR'` âˆ’ Î£ where `'DB'`. Tolerance `min(0.10, max(0.01, 0.005Â·âˆšlines))` | OK / ALERT. INFO only when the account range is not the default one |
| C2 | Balance formula | for every row: `PREVIOUS_BALANCE + (Â±AMOUNT_ACCOUNT_CCY) = BALANCE` (`+` for CR, `âˆ’` for DB), tolerance 0.005 | OK if 0 rows differ |
| C3 | Balance chaining | per position (account, rubric, currency, maturity, `PTF_MANAGER`) ordered by (`ENTRY_NEXT`, `N_LOT`, `N_LINE`): each row's `PREVIOUS_BALANCE` = the previous row's `BALANCE` | OK if 0 breaks |
| C4 | Final balance | per position, the `BALANCE_ACCOUNT_CCY` of the last row (highest `ENTRY_NEXT`, `N_LOT`, `N_LINE`) = Q35 `BALANCE_MIN` = `BALANCE_MAX` | OK if all positions match |

### 6.3 Errors (all in user language, none retried)

| Situation | Error |
|---|---|
| Invalid parameter or forbidden combination | rejected before any query (see 1.4) |
| Q00 returns no row | fund not found in Table Fonds |
| Q00 `EFRONT = '1'` | fund refused (eFront) |
| Q01 returns null | no NAV for this calculation date |
| Q10â€“Q16 return no row | no lot for this NAV |
| Q15 returns no row | no NAV on or before `date_to` |
| Q18 returns no row | no controlled / published NAV for this mode at `TODAY` |
| Any query returns more than the row cap | failure, never truncation |

### 7.3 BCR â€” 19 columns, in this order

| # | Column header | Q20 alias | Type / format |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `SubFund Number` | `SUBFUND_NUMBER` | text |
| 2 | `SubFund Name` | `SUBFUND_NAME` | text |
| 3 | `SubFund Ccy` | `SUBFUND_CCY` | text |
| 4 | `Account Number` | `ACCOUNT_NUMBER` | integer |
| 5 | `Sub-Account Number` | `ACCOUNT_RUBRIC` | text (not numerically reformatted) |
| 6 | `Account Name` | `ACCOUNT_NAME` | text |
| 7 | `Account Ccy` | `ACCOUNT_CCY` | text |
| 8 | `Debit / Credit` | `DEBIT_CREDIT` | text, `DB` or `CR` |
| 9 | `Service Code` | `CODE_SERVICE` | text |
| 10 | `Operation Code` | `OPERATION_CODE` | text |
| 11 | `Accounting Date` | `ACCOUNTING_DATE` | date |
| 12 | `Trade Date` | `TRADE_DATE` | date |
| 13 | `Value Date` | `VALUE_DATE` | date |
| 14 | `Description` | `DESCRIPTION` | text |
| 15 | `Entry` | `ENTRY` | integer |
| 16 | `Entry Ptf` | `ENTRY_PTF` | integer |
| 17 | `Amount in Account Ccy` | `AMOUNT_ACCOUNT_CCY` | decimal |
| 18 | `Amount in SubFund Ccy` | `AMOUNT_SUBFUND_CCY` | decimal |
| 19 | `Status` | `STATUS` | integer |

BCR does **not** carry `Maturity Date`, `Entry Next`, `Previous Balance in Account Ccy`, `Balance in Account Ccy` (those aliases are still in the Q20 rows, used by the controls).

### 7.4 CSV format (LUXIS native, the reference format)

| Aspect | Value |
|---|---|
| Header | first line, the column headers above, separated by `;` |
| Separator | `;` |
| Quoting | **none** (LUXIS writes no quotes). A `;`, CR or LF inside a text value is replaced by a space so the file does not break |
| Encoding | ANSI `cp1252`; characters not representable are replaced |
| Line ending | `CRLF` (`\r\n`); no line ending after the last row |
| Dates | `dd.MM.yyyy` (e.g. `29.06.2026`); a null date is empty |
| Integers / decimals | decimal point, no thousands separator, no trailing zeros (`100.5`, `0`, `-12.34`); a null value is empty |
| Apostrophes `'` | removed from every text value and from the header |
| Nulls | empty field |

Date columns are `Accounting Date`, `Trade Date`, `Value Date`, `Maturity Date`. Numeric columns are `Account Number`, `Account Rubric` (IRP only), `Entry`, `Entry Ptf`, `Entry Next`, `Status` and the four amount / balance columns.

Plain CSV variant (when LUXIS-style is not needed): UTF-8 with BOM, `;` separator, `csv` module quoting rules, dates `YYYY-MM-DD`, integers without decimals, amounts as decimals.

### 7.5 File name

`{fund} - GeneralLedger-{YYYY_MM_DD}_{HH_MM_SS_cc}` with **all spaces removed**, then `.csv`.

- `YYYY_MM_DD` = date of the NAV: `nav` for IRP single-NAV; otherwise `NAV_TO` of the window; `date_to` as the last resort.
- `HH_MM_SS_cc` = generation time, `cc` = hundredths of a second.
- No prefix by default.

Example: `242013-GeneralLedger-2026_06_29_10_45_39_74.csv`

### 7.6 Same file, xlsx

Not specified here (handled by the other tool). The same 23 / 19 columns apply, sheet name `A`, built from a LUXIS template.

# General Ledger on Dremio layers â€” proposed lineage

Companion to `specs.md`. `specs.md` describes the queries as they run **today** (the application reads the source tables and carries the logic in 10+ chained queries). This document proposes the **target design**: all the logic moves into Dremio views, and the application only runs `SELECT * â€¦ WHERE â€¦` on a thin application layer.

> **Status: proposal.** The view definitions below were derived from the existing queries in `sql/*.sql` and from `specs.md`. None of them has been created or executed on Dremio. Dremio syntax (`LAST_DAY`, `TIMESTAMPADD`, `DATE_TRUNC`, window functions in views) and performance must be validated on INTG and CTLQ. Section 8 lists what is unproven.

## 1. Principles

| Layer | Dremio space | Content | Logic allowed |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Source** | `MFGA_INFOCENTRE`, `LUXIS`, â€¦ | The systems' own tables. **Not read by the application** | â€“ |
| **Staging** | `STAGGING` (two G, Dremio's spelling) | One 1:1 replica of each source table | **None.** No filter, no rename, no join |
| **Business** | `BUSINESS` | Everything that is business or intelligence: NAV calendars, period windows, closings, previous balance, account names, result-account flag, constants (`40000`, plan `'20'`), the backdated-NAV rule | **All of it**, and no parameter: a view never knows the report's input |
| **Application** | `APPLICATION` | One view per thing the application needs, each a plain projection of one business view | **None.** `SELECT â€¦ FROM BUSINESSâ€¦` |

The application (the other tool) then does only this:

1. `SELECT * FROM APPLICATION.â€¦ WHERE <the user's values>`
2. a fixed `ORDER BY` on the entries
3. hand one result's values to the next `WHERE` (for example the lot window)

Rules that make this work:

- **A view exposes everything, for every fund and every date.** The user's values select rows with `WHERE`. This is why the business views carry *validity intervals* (`NAV_DATE` â€¦ `NEXT_NAV_DATE`) and *precomputed per-period windows* instead of taking a date as a parameter.
- **A filter on `FUND_NUMBER` must always be present** in an application statement (it is the pushdown key of every view).
- **No new intelligence in `APPLICATION`.** The existing `APPLICATION.BETIS.GeneralLedgers` is already a bare `select *` of a business view (see `docs/CHAINAGE-DONNEES.md` Â§8, blocking point C); this design follows the same pattern.

Schema folder used below: `GENERAL_LEDGER` in each space. Names are proposals.

---

## 3. Staging layer â€” 1:1 replicas

One replica per source table, named after the table, columns and types untouched. Where the platform already replicates a table in `STAGGING`, reuse it; the paths below are the ones known from `config/defaults.json` and `docs/CHAINAGE-DONNEES.md` and **must be confirmed with the platform team**.

| Proposed staging object | Source | Already in `STAGGING`? |
|---|---|---|
| `STAGGING.GENERAL_LEDGER.AMS_LOT` | `MFGA_INFOCENTRE.DWH.AMS_LOT` | to confirm |
| `STAGGING.GENERAL_LEDGER.AMS_CASH_MVT` | `MFGA_INFOCENTRE.DWH.AMS_CASH_MVT` | **not found**: `BUSINESSâ€¦GENERAL_LEDGERS` reads `STAGGING.LDR.CORE.AMS.HMT` instead, which has no lot column (blocking point B). A DWH replica is needed |
| `STAGGING.GENERAL_LEDGER.AMS_PORTFOLIO` | `MFGA_INFOCENTRE.DWH.AMS_PORTFOLIO` | `STAGGING.LDR.DWH.AMS.AMS_PORTFOLIO` |
| `STAGGING.GENERAL_LEDGER.AMS_ACC_DEF` | `MFGA_INFOCENTRE.DWH.AMS_ACC_DEF` | to confirm |
| `STAGGING.GENERAL_LEDGER.AMS_ACC_POS` | `MFGA_INFOCENTRE.DWH.AMS_ACC_POS` | to confirm (`POSITION_PER_ACCOUNT` reads `PIC_AMS_ACC_POS`, a different table) |
| `STAGGING.GENERAL_LEDGER.TAB_FND_MAIN` | `LUXIS.REPADMIN.TAB_FND_MAIN` | to confirm (`BUSINESSâ€¦tab_fnd_main` is missing on CTLQ) |
| `STAGGING.GENERAL_LEDGER.NAV` | `LUXIS.REPADMIN.NAV` | `STAGGING.LXS.REPADMIN.NAV` |

Each staging view is literally:

```sql
CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW STAGGING.GENERAL_LEDGER.AMS_LOT AS
SELECT * FROM MFGA_INFOCENTRE.DWH.AMS_LOT;
```

(and the same shape for the six others).

Columns the business layer reads:

## 4. Business layer â€” where the logic lives

All views are parameter-free and cover every fund and every date. Constants that were passed as parameters or configuration (`40000`, plan `'20'`) are now written **once**, here.

### 4.1 `FUND` â€” fund sheet (replaces Q00)

One row per fund. Flags are computed, not interpreted by the application.

```sql
CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW BUSINESS.GENERAL_LEDGER.FUND AS
SELECT t.FA_NUM                       AS FUND_NUMBER,
       MIN(t.FUND_NAME)               AS FUND_NAME,
       MIN(t.FUND_CCY)                AS FUND_CCY,
       CASE WHEN MAX(CAST(t.EFRONT AS VARCHAR)) = '1' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END                         AS IS_EFRONT,
       CASE WHEN COALESCE(MAX(CAST(t.NAV_BACKDATED AS INTEGER)), 2) <> 2 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END      AS IS_NAV_BACKDATED
FROM STAGGING.GENERAL_LEDGER.TAB_FND_MAIN t
GROUP BY t.FA_NUM;
```

### 4.2 `FUND_FIRST_NAV` â€” first NAV with shares (feeds periods 13, 14, 15, 16 without closing)

```sql
CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW BUSINESS.GENERAL_LEDGER.FUND_FIRST_NAV AS
SELECT n.NAV_FUND_NO AS FUND_NUMBER, CAST(MIN(n.NAV_DATE_NAV) AS DATE) AS FIRST_NAV_DATE
FROM STAGGING.GENERAL_LEDGER.NAV n
WHERE n.NAV_QT_TOT_PART <> 0
GROUP BY n.NAV_FUND_NO;
```

### 4.3 `NAV_CALENDAR` â€” the three NAV calendars with their lot bounds (replaces Q01, Q15, Q18 and the `cal` / `debut` CTEs of Q10â€“Q16)

One row per fund per NAV date, in **three calendars** (`CALENDAR_TYPE`):

| `CALENDAR_TYPE` | NAV dates taken from | Used by |
|---|---|---|
| `LOTS` | the lots table (`AMS_LOT.D_NAV`) | IRP periods, IRP range, BCR `plage` |
| `CONTROLLED` | the NAV table, `NAV_CONTROLE = 'Y'` | BCR `last_available_day` |
| `PUBLISHED` | the NAV table, `NAV_PUB = 'A'` | BCR `to_last_date_nav` |

Every row carries a **validity interval**: the row is "the last NAV on or before date *d*" when `NAV_DATE <= d AND NEXT_NAV_DATE > d`. That is how "last NAV on or before a date" becomes a plain `WHERE`.

| Column | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `CALENDAR_TYPE`, `FUND_NUMBER`, `NAV_DATE` | key |
| `PREV_NAV_DATE` | previous NAV of the same calendar, null for the first |
| `PREV_NAV_KEY` | same, but `1900-01-01` instead of null, so it can be used in range predicates |
| `NEXT_NAV_DATE` | next NAV of the same calendar, `9999-12-31` for the last |
| `CALC_DATE` | processing day of the last lot of the NAV (used to turn a calculation date into a NAV) |
| `LOT_START` | lot to use as **exclusive lower bound when this NAV is the start NAV**: last lot of the NAV, or its smallest lot if the fund has backdated NAVs, or `0` if the NAV has no lot |
| `PREV_LOT_START` | `LOT_START` of the previous NAV of the same calendar (the lower bound of the window "since previous NAV") |
| `LOT_END` | last lot of the NAV (inclusive upper bound), `0` if the NAV has no lot |
| `TRADE_DATE_MAX` | `NAV_DATE` for a backdated fund, `9999-12-31` otherwise |

```sql
CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW BUSINESS.GENERAL_LEDGER.NAV_CALENDAR AS
WITH lot_cal AS (
  SELECT l.C_FUND AS FUND_NUMBER, CAST(l.D_NAV AS DATE) AS NAV_DATE,
         MIN(l.N_LOT) AS LOT_MIN, MAX(l.N_LOT) AS LOT_MAX
  FROM STAGGING.GENERAL_LEDGER.AMS_LOT l
  GROUP BY l.C_FUND, CAST(l.D_NAV AS DATE)),
last_lot AS (
  SELECT x.FUND_NUMBER, x.NAV_DATE, x.CALC_DATE
  FROM (SELECT l.C_FUND AS FUND_NUMBER, CAST(l.D_NAV AS DATE) AS NAV_DATE,
               CAST(l.D_H_PROCESS AS DATE) AS CALC_DATE,
               ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY l.C_FUND, CAST(l.D_NAV AS DATE) ORDER BY l.N_LOT DESC) AS RN
        FROM STAGGING.GENERAL_LEDGER.AMS_LOT l) x
  WHERE x.RN = 1),
nav_all AS (
  SELECT 'LOTS' AS CALENDAR_TYPE, FUND_NUMBER, NAV_DATE FROM lot_cal
  UNION ALL
  SELECT 'CONTROLLED', n.NAV_FUND_NO, CAST(n.NAV_DATE_NAV AS DATE)
  FROM STAGGING.GENERAL_LEDGER.NAV n WHERE n.NAV_CONTROLE = 'Y'
  UNION ALL
  SELECT 'PUBLISHED', n.NAV_FUND_NO, CAST(n.NAV_DATE_NAV AS DATE)
  FROM STAGGING.GENERAL_LEDGER.NAV n WHERE n.NAV_PUB = 'A'),
dated AS (
  SELECT d.CALENDAR_TYPE, d.FUND_NUMBER, d.NAV_DATE,
         COALESCE(CASE WHEN f.IS_NAV_BACKDATED = 1 THEN lc.LOT_MIN ELSE lc.LOT_MAX END, 0) AS LOT_START,
         COALESCE(lc.LOT_MAX, 0)                                                              AS LOT_END,
         CASE WHEN f.IS_NAV_BACKDATED = 1 THEN d.NAV_DATE ELSE DATE '9999-12-31' END         AS TRADE_DATE_MAX
  FROM (SELECT DISTINCT CALENDAR_TYPE, FUND_NUMBER, NAV_DATE FROM nav_all) d
  LEFT JOIN lot_cal lc ON lc.FUND_NUMBER = d.FUND_NUMBER AND lc.NAV_DATE = d.NAV_DATE
  LEFT JOIN BUSINESS.GENERAL_LEDGER.FUND f ON f.FUND_NUMBER = d.FUND_NUMBER)
SELECT s.CALENDAR_TYPE, s.FUND_NUMBER, s.NAV_DATE,
       s.PREV_NAV_DATE,
       COALESCE(s.PREV_NAV_DATE, DATE '1900-01-01') AS PREV_NAV_KEY,
       s.NEXT_NAV_DATE,
       ll.CALC_DATE,
       s.LOT_START, s.PREV_LOT_START, s.LOT_END, s.TRADE_DATE_MAX
FROM (SELECT d.*,
             LAG(d.NAV_DATE)       OVER (PARTITION BY d.CALENDAR_TYPE, d.FUND_NUMBER ORDER BY d.NAV_DATE) AS PREV_NAV_DATE,
             LAG(d.LOT_START)      OVER (PARTITION BY d.CALENDAR_TYPE, d.FUND_NUMBER ORDER BY d.NAV_DATE) AS PREV_LOT_START,
             COALESCE(LEAD(d.NAV_DATE) OVER (PARTITION BY d.CALENDAR_TYPE, d.FUND_NUMBER ORDER BY d.NAV_DATE),
                      DATE '9999-12-31') AS NEXT_NAV_DATE
      FROM dated d) s
LEFT JOIN last_lot ll ON ll.FUND_NUMBER = s.FUND_NUMBER AND ll.NAV_DATE = s.NAV_DATE;
```

Edge case kept from the original rules: a NAV date of the `CONTROLLED` or `PUBLISHED` calendar with no lot gets `LOT_START = 0` and `LOT_END = 0` (LUXIS `GET_LOT_DATE_NAV(â€¦, 0)`).

### 4.4 `FUND_CLOSING` â€” every annual closing of every fund (replaces Q02, first half)

A closing is a service `RS` entry on a result account that is valid (status 20), not reversed (no status 30 on the same account and entry), and the last of its accounting day and account. The closing lot is the last lot of the fund strictly before the `RS` lot. Constants `40000`, `47410`, `57410`, `999998` are business rules and live here.

```sql
CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW BUSINESS.GENERAL_LEDGER.FUND_CLOSING AS
WITH t AS (
  SELECT c.C_FUND, c.N_LOT, c.N_ENTRY, CAST(c.D_ACC AS DATE) AS D_ACC, c.C_N_ACC, c.R_EXCHANGE, c.C_STATUS
  FROM STAGGING.GENERAL_LEDGER.AMS_CASH_MVT c
  WHERE c.C_SRV = 'RS'),
rs AS (
  SELECT t.* FROM t
  WHERE t.C_N_ACC >= 40000 AND t.C_N_ACC NOT IN (47410, 57410, 999998)
    AND t.R_EXCHANGE <> 0 AND t.C_STATUS = 20),
maxlot AS (
  SELECT t.C_FUND, t.D_ACC, t.C_N_ACC, MAX(t.N_LOT) AS ML FROM t GROUP BY t.C_FUND, t.D_ACC, t.C_N_ACC),
rev AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT t.C_FUND, t.C_N_ACC, t.N_ENTRY FROM t WHERE t.C_STATUS = 30),
cand AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT rs.C_FUND, rs.N_LOT
  FROM rs
  JOIN maxlot m ON m.C_FUND = rs.C_FUND AND m.D_ACC = rs.D_ACC AND m.C_N_ACC = rs.C_N_ACC AND m.ML = rs.N_LOT
  LEFT JOIN rev r ON r.C_FUND = rs.C_FUND AND r.C_N_ACC = rs.C_N_ACC AND r.N_ENTRY = rs.N_ENTRY
  WHERE r.N_ENTRY IS NULL),
lots AS (
  SELECT l.C_FUND, l.N_LOT, CAST(l.D_NAV AS DATE) AS D_NAV FROM STAGGING.GENERAL_LEDGER.AMS_LOT l),
clot AS (
  SELECT c.C_FUND, c.N_LOT AS LOT_RS, MAX(l.N_LOT) AS LOT_CLOT
  FROM cand c JOIN lots l ON l.C_FUND = c.C_FUND AND l.N_LOT < c.N_LOT
  GROUP BY c.C_FUND, c.N_LOT)
SELECT k.C_FUND AS FUND_NUMBER, k.LOT_RS, lr.D_NAV AS RS_NAV_DATE,
       k.LOT_CLOT, lc.D_NAV AS CLOSING_NAV_DATE
FROM clot k
JOIN lots lc ON lc.C_FUND = k.C_FUND AND lc.N_LOT = k.LOT_CLOT
JOIN lots lr ON lr.C_FUND = k.C_FUND AND lr.N_LOT = k.LOT_RS;
```

### 4.5 `NAV_LAST_CLOSING` â€” the closing in force at each NAV (replaces Q02, second half)

For each NAV of the lots calendar, the latest closing whose `RS` lot belongs to that NAV or an earlier one and whose closing NAV is strictly before the NAV. No row = no closing.

```sql
CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW BUSINESS.GENERAL_LEDGER.NAV_LAST_CLOSING AS
SELECT x.FUND_NUMBER, x.NAV_DATE, x.CLOSING_LOT, x.CLOSING_NAV
FROM (SELECT c.FUND_NUMBER, c.NAV_DATE, k.LOT_CLOT AS CLOSING_LOT, k.CLOSING_NAV_DATE AS CLOSING_NAV,
             ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY c.FUND_NUMBER, c.NAV_DATE ORDER BY k.LOT_RS DESC) AS RN
      FROM BUSINESS.GENERAL_LEDGER.NAV_CALENDAR c
      JOIN BUSINESS.GENERAL_LEDGER.FUND_CLOSING k
        ON k.FUND_NUMBER = c.FUND_NUMBER
       AND k.RS_NAV_DATE <= c.NAV_DATE
       AND k.CLOSING_NAV_DATE < c.NAV_DATE
      WHERE c.CALENDAR_TYPE = 'LOTS') x
WHERE x.RN = 1;
```

### 4.6 `PERIOD_WINDOW` â€” lot window for each (fund, NAV, period) (replaces Q10, Q11, Q12, Q13, Q14, Q16)

One row per fund, NAV date of the lots calendar and `PERIOD_CODE` 1â€“16. The application selects the single row it needs.

| Column | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `FUND_NUMBER`, `NAV_DATE` (= `NAV_TO`), `PERIOD_CODE` | key |
| `NAV_FROM` | start NAV of the period (null when none) |
| `LOT_FROM` | exclusive lower lot bound (`0` for period 16 and when no start NAV) |
| `LOT_TO` | inclusive upper lot bound |
| `TRADE_DATE_MAX` | `NAV_DATE` for a backdated fund, `9999-12-31` otherwise |
| `RESULT_LOT_FROM`, `RESULT_DATE_FROM` | the filter for **result accounts** (â‰¥ 40000): period 16 with a closing â†’ closing lot and closing NAV; every other case â†’ `0` and `1900-01-01` (neutral) |
| `HAS_CLOSING` | 1 if a closing exists before this NAV |

The rules are the corrected rule set of `specs.md` (periods 13 and 16):

| Period | `NAV_FROM` |
|---|---|
| 1 | `PREV_NAV_DATE` |
| 2 | last NAV â‰¤ NAV âˆ’ 7 days |
| 3 | last NAV â‰¤ NAV âˆ’ 14 days |
| 4â€“8 | last NAV â‰¤ NAV âˆ’ 1, 2, 3, 6, 12 months (Oracle `ADD_MONTHS` rule) |
| 9, 10, 11, 12 | last NAV â‰¤ end of previous month / quarter / half-year / year |
| 13 and 14 | closing NAV if a closing exists, else first NAV with shares (corrected rule: 13 = 14) |
| 15 | first NAV with shares |
| 16 | closing NAV (null if none); `LOT_FROM = 0`; result accounts filtered by closing lot and closing NAV |

```sql
CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW BUSINESS.GENERAL_LEDGER.PERIOD_WINDOW AS
WITH cal AS (
  SELECT * FROM BUSINESS.GENERAL_LEDGER.NAV_CALENDAR WHERE CALENDAR_TYPE = 'LOTS'),
base AS (
  SELECT c.FUND_NUMBER, c.NAV_DATE, c.PREV_NAV_DATE, k.CLOSING_LOT, k.CLOSING_NAV, fn.FIRST_NAV_DATE
  FROM cal c
  LEFT JOIN BUSINESS.GENERAL_LEDGER.NAV_LAST_CLOSING k ON k.FUND_NUMBER = c.FUND_NUMBER AND k.NAV_DATE = c.NAV_DATE
  LEFT JOIN BUSINESS.GENERAL_LEDGER.FUND_FIRST_NAV  fn ON fn.FUND_NUMBER = c.FUND_NUMBER),
target AS (   -- periods 2-12: target date; the start NAV is the last NAV on or before it
  SELECT FUND_NUMBER, NAV_DATE, 2 AS PERIOD_CODE, CAST(CAST(NAV_DATE AS TIMESTAMP) - INTERVAL '7' DAY AS DATE) AS TARGET_DATE FROM base
  UNION ALL SELECT FUND_NUMBER, NAV_DATE, 3, CAST(CAST(NAV_DATE AS TIMESTAMP) - INTERVAL '14' DAY AS DATE) FROM base
  UNION ALL SELECT FUND_NUMBER, NAV_DATE, 4,  CAST(CASE WHEN NAV_DATE = LAST_DAY(NAV_DATE) THEN LAST_DAY(TIMESTAMPADD(MONTH, -1,  CAST(NAV_DATE AS TIMESTAMP))) ELSE TIMESTAMPADD(MONTH, -1,  CAST(NAV_DATE AS TIMESTAMP)) END AS DATE) FROM base
  UNION ALL SELECT FUND_NUMBER, NAV_DATE, 5,  CAST(CASE WHEN NAV_DATE = LAST_DAY(NAV_DATE) THEN LAST_DAY(TIMESTAMPADD(MONTH, -2,  CAST(NAV_DATE AS TIMESTAMP))) ELSE TIMESTAMPADD(MONTH, -2,  CAST(NAV_DATE AS TIMESTAMP)) END AS DATE) FROM base
  UNION ALL SELECT FUND_NUMBER, NAV_DATE, 6,  CAST(CASE WHEN NAV_DATE = LAST_DAY(NAV_DATE) THEN LAST_DAY(TIMESTAMPADD(MONTH, -3,  CAST(NAV_DATE AS TIMESTAMP))) ELSE TIMESTAMPADD(MONTH, -3,  CAST(NAV_DATE AS TIMESTAMP)) END AS DATE) FROM base
  UNION ALL SELECT FUND_NUMBER, NAV_DATE, 7,  CAST(CASE WHEN NAV_DATE = LAST_DAY(NAV_DATE) THEN LAST_DAY(TIMESTAMPADD(MONTH, -6,  CAST(NAV_DATE AS TIMESTAMP))) ELSE TIMESTAMPADD(MONTH, -6,  CAST(NAV_DATE AS TIMESTAMP)) END AS DATE) FROM base
  UNION ALL SELECT FUND_NUMBER, NAV_DATE, 8,  CAST(CASE WHEN NAV_DATE = LAST_DAY(NAV_DATE) THEN LAST_DAY(TIMESTAMPADD(MONTH, -12, CAST(NAV_DATE AS TIMESTAMP))) ELSE TIMESTAMPADD(MONTH, -12, CAST(NAV_DATE AS TIMESTAMP)) END AS DATE) FROM base
  UNION ALL SELECT FUND_NUMBER, NAV_DATE, 9,  CAST(CAST(DATE_TRUNC('MONTH',   NAV_DATE) AS TIMESTAMP) - INTERVAL '1' DAY AS DATE) FROM base
  UNION ALL SELECT FUND_NUMBER, NAV_DATE, 10, CAST(CAST(DATE_TRUNC('QUARTER', NAV_DATE) AS TIMESTAMP) - INTERVAL '1' DAY AS DATE) FROM base
  UNION ALL SELECT FUND_NUMBER, NAV_DATE, 11,
         CAST(CASE WHEN EXTRACT(MONTH FROM NAV_DATE) < 7
                   THEN CAST(DATE_TRUNC('YEAR', NAV_DATE) AS TIMESTAMP) - INTERVAL '1' DAY
                   ELSE TIMESTAMPADD(MONTH, 6, CAST(DATE_TRUNC('YEAR', NAV_DATE) AS TIMESTAMP)) - INTERVAL '1' DAY END AS DATE) FROM base
  UNION ALL SELECT FUND_NUMBER, NAV_DATE, 12, CAST(CAST(DATE_TRUNC('YEAR', NAV_DATE) AS TIMESTAMP) - INTERVAL '1' DAY AS DATE) FROM base),
start_nav AS (
  SELECT FUND_NUMBER, NAV_DATE, 1  AS PERIOD_CODE, PREV_NAV_DATE                              AS NAV_FROM FROM base
  UNION ALL
  SELECT t.FUND_NUMBER, t.NAV_DATE, t.PERIOD_CODE, s.NAV_DATE
  FROM target t
  LEFT JOIN cal s ON s.FUND_NUMBER = t.FUND_NUMBER AND s.NAV_DATE <= t.TARGET_DATE AND s.NEXT_NAV_DATE > t.TARGET_DATE
  UNION ALL SELECT FUND_NUMBER, NAV_DATE, 13, COALESCE(CLOSING_NAV, FIRST_NAV_DATE) FROM base
  UNION ALL SELECT FUND_NUMBER, NAV_DATE, 14, COALESCE(CLOSING_NAV, FIRST_NAV_DATE) FROM base
  UNION ALL SELECT FUND_NUMBER, NAV_DATE, 15, FIRST_NAV_DATE                         FROM base
  UNION ALL SELECT FUND_NUMBER, NAV_DATE, 16, CLOSING_NAV                            FROM base)
SELECT n.FUND_NUMBER, n.NAV_DATE, n.PERIOD_CODE, n.NAV_FROM,
       CASE WHEN n.PERIOD_CODE = 16 THEN 0 ELSE COALESCE(f.LOT_START, 0) END AS LOT_FROM,
       a.LOT_END           AS LOT_TO,
       a.TRADE_DATE_MAX    AS TRADE_DATE_MAX,
       CASE WHEN n.PERIOD_CODE = 16 AND b.CLOSING_LOT IS NOT NULL THEN b.CLOSING_LOT ELSE 0 END                 AS RESULT_LOT_FROM,
       CASE WHEN n.PERIOD_CODE = 16 AND b.CLOSING_LOT IS NOT NULL THEN b.CLOSING_NAV ELSE DATE '1900-01-01' END AS RESULT_DATE_FROM,
       CASE WHEN b.CLOSING_LOT IS NULL THEN 0 ELSE 1 END                                                       AS HAS_CLOSING
FROM start_nav n
JOIN cal  a ON a.FUND_NUMBER = n.FUND_NUMBER AND a.NAV_DATE = n.NAV_DATE
JOIN base b ON b.FUND_NUMBER = n.FUND_NUMBER AND b.NAV_DATE = n.NAV_DATE
LEFT JOIN cal f ON f.FUND_NUMBER = n.FUND_NUMBER AND f.NAV_DATE = n.NAV_FROM AND f.NAV_DATE <= n.NAV_DATE;
```

Notes: the last join keeps the original behaviour that the start NAV is looked up only among NAVs up to the requested NAV; the 16 periods are stacked with `UNION ALL` (never a join on a `VALUES` list: Dremio truncates those silently, see `sql/20_ecritures.sql`).

### 4.7 `FUND_PLAN` and `ACCOUNT_NAME` â€” account labels (replace the `plan` and `noms` CTEs of Q20)

```sql
CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW BUSINESS.GENERAL_LEDGER.FUND_PLAN AS   -- chart of accounts of each fund = plan of its latest lot
SELECT x.C_FUND AS FUND_NUMBER, x.C_ACC_PLAN AS ACC_PLAN
FROM (SELECT p.C_FUND, p.C_ACC_PLAN,
             ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY p.C_FUND ORDER BY p.N_LOT DESC) AS RN
      FROM STAGGING.GENERAL_LEDGER.AMS_PORTFOLIO p) x
WHERE x.RN = 1;

CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW BUSINESS.GENERAL_LEDGER.ACCOUNT_NAME AS   -- latest version (highest lot) of each account name in each plan
SELECT x.C_ACC_PLAN AS ACC_PLAN, x.C_N_ACC AS ACCOUNT_NUMBER, x.L_NAME AS ACCOUNT_NAME
FROM (SELECT d.C_ACC_PLAN, d.C_N_ACC, d.L_NAME,
             ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY d.C_ACC_PLAN, d.C_N_ACC ORDER BY d.N_LOT DESC) AS RN
      FROM STAGGING.GENERAL_LEDGER.AMS_ACC_DEF d) x
WHERE x.RN = 1;
```

### 4.8 `ENTRY` â€” the ledger lines, ready for both reports (replaces Q20)

One row per entry of every fund. Everything the reports show, plus the columns that let the application filter and order with plain `WHERE` / `ORDER BY`:

- **Fund name and currency** come from `FUND`.
- **Account name**: two columns, because the two reports differ â€” `ACCOUNT_NAME_FUND_PLAN` (IRP: the fund's own chart of accounts) and `ACCOUNT_NAME_BCR_PLAN` (BCR: chart `'20'`, which LuxRep hard-codes).
- **`PREVIOUS_BALANCE_ACCOUNT_CCY`** is computed here.
- **`IS_RESULT_ACCOUNT`** = account â‰¥ 40000. The threshold lives here, not in the application.
- **`TRADE_DATE_FILTER`** = the trade date for a backdated fund, `1900-01-01` otherwise. Combined with `PERIOD_WINDOW.TRADE_DATE_MAX`, the application's condition `TRADE_DATE_FILTER <= TRADE_DATE_MAX` is a no-op for ordinary funds and the LUXIS trade-date rule for backdated funds.
- **`SORT_*`** columns: the numeric keys of the LUXIS ordering (cast to `DOUBLE`, null = 0).
- Only entries whose lot exists in the fund's lots are kept (the semi-join of the original query).

```sql
CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW BUSINESS.GENERAL_LEDGER.ENTRY AS
SELECT c.C_FUND                 AS FUND_NUMBER,
       f.FUND_NAME              AS FUND_NAME,
       f.FUND_CCY               AS FUND_CCY,
       c.C_N_ACC                AS ACCOUNT_NUMBER,
       c.N_SUF                  AS ACCOUNT_RUBRIC,
       nf.ACCOUNT_NAME          AS ACCOUNT_NAME_FUND_PLAN,
       nb.ACCOUNT_NAME          AS ACCOUNT_NAME_BCR_PLAN,
       c.C_CCY                  AS ACCOUNT_CCY,
       c.C_ACC_WAY              AS DEBIT_CREDIT,
       c.C_SRV                  AS CODE_SERVICE,
       c.C_OPE                  AS OPERATION_CODE,
       c.D_ACC                  AS ACCOUNTING_DATE,
       c.D_TRADE                AS TRADE_DATE,
       c.D_VALUE                AS VALUE_DATE,
       c.D_MATURITY             AS MATURITY_DATE,
       c.L_MVT                  AS DESCRIPTION,
       c.N_ENTRY                AS ENTRY,
       c.N_ENTRY_PTF            AS ENTRY_PTF,
       c."N_NEXT"               AS ENTRY_NEXT,
       c.A_MVT                  AS AMOUNT_ACCOUNT_CCY,
       c.A_MVT_PTF              AS AMOUNT_SUBFUND_CCY,
       CASE WHEN c.C_ACC_WAY = 'CR' THEN c.A_BALANCE - c.A_MVT ELSE c.A_BALANCE + c.A_MVT END AS PREVIOUS_BALANCE_ACCOUNT_CCY,
       c.A_BALANCE              AS BALANCE_ACCOUNT_CCY,
       c.C_STATUS               AS STATUS,
       c.N_LOT                  AS N_LOT,
       c.N_LINE                 AS N_LINE,
       c.C_N_PTF_MANAGER        AS PTF_MANAGER,
       CASE WHEN c.C_N_ACC >= 40000 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END                                          AS IS_RESULT_ACCOUNT,
       CASE WHEN f.IS_NAV_BACKDATED = 1 THEN c.D_TRADE ELSE TIMESTAMP '1900-01-01 00:00:00' END AS TRADE_DATE_FILTER,
       COALESCE(CAST(c.C_N_ACC      AS DOUBLE), 0) AS SORT_ACCOUNT,
       COALESCE(CAST(c.N_SUF        AS DOUBLE), 0) AS SORT_RUBRIC,
       COALESCE(CAST(c."N_NEXT"     AS DOUBLE), 0) AS SORT_NEXT,
       COALESCE(CAST(c.N_ENTRY      AS DOUBLE), 0) AS SORT_ENTRY,
       COALESCE(CAST(c.N_ENTRY_PTF  AS DOUBLE), 0) AS SORT_ENTRY_PTF,
       COALESCE(CAST(c.N_LOT        AS DOUBLE), 0) AS SORT_LOT,
       COALESCE(CAST(c.N_LINE       AS DOUBLE), 0) AS SORT_LINE,
       COALESCE(CAST(c.A_MVT        AS DOUBLE), 0) AS SORT_AMOUNT
FROM STAGGING.GENERAL_LEDGER.AMS_CASH_MVT c
LEFT JOIN BUSINESS.GENERAL_LEDGER.FUND         f  ON f.FUND_NUMBER = c.C_FUND
LEFT JOIN BUSINESS.GENERAL_LEDGER.FUND_PLAN    p  ON p.FUND_NUMBER = c.C_FUND
LEFT JOIN BUSINESS.GENERAL_LEDGER.ACCOUNT_NAME nf ON nf.ACC_PLAN = p.ACC_PLAN AND nf.ACCOUNT_NUMBER = c.C_N_ACC
LEFT JOIN BUSINESS.GENERAL_LEDGER.ACCOUNT_NAME nb ON nb.ACC_PLAN = '20'       AND nb.ACCOUNT_NUMBER = c.C_N_ACC
WHERE EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM STAGGING.GENERAL_LEDGER.AMS_LOT l WHERE l.C_FUND = c.C_FUND AND l.N_LOT = c.N_LOT);
```

### 4.9 `POSITION_BALANCE` â€” balances at each lot (replaces Q35, control only)

```sql
CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW BUSINESS.GENERAL_LEDGER.POSITION_BALANCE AS
SELECT p.C_FUND AS FUND_NUMBER, p.N_LOT, p.C_N_ACC AS ACCOUNT_NUMBER, p.N_SUF AS ACCOUNT_RUBRIC,
       p.C_ACC_CCY AS ACCOUNT_CCY, p.D_MATURITY AS MATURITY_DATE, p.C_N_PTF_MANAGER AS PTF_MANAGER,
       MIN(p.A_BALANCE) AS BALANCE_MIN, MAX(p.A_BALANCE) AS BALANCE_MAX, COUNT(*) AS N_LIGNES
FROM STAGGING.GENERAL_LEDGER.AMS_ACC_POS p
GROUP BY p.C_FUND, p.N_LOT, p.C_N_ACC, p.N_SUF, p.C_ACC_CCY, p.D_MATURITY, p.C_N_PTF_MANAGER;
```

## 5. Application layer â€” projections only

Each application view is a bare projection of one business view. No filter, no join, no expression.

```sql
CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW APPLICATION.GENERAL_LEDGER.FUND             AS SELECT * FROM BUSINESS.GENERAL_LEDGER.FUND;
CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW APPLICATION.GENERAL_LEDGER.NAV_CALENDAR     AS SELECT * FROM BUSINESS.GENERAL_LEDGER.NAV_CALENDAR;
CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW APPLICATION.GENERAL_LEDGER.PERIOD_WINDOW    AS SELECT * FROM BUSINESS.GENERAL_LEDGER.PERIOD_WINDOW;
CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW APPLICATION.GENERAL_LEDGER.POSITION_BALANCE AS SELECT * FROM BUSINESS.GENERAL_LEDGER.POSITION_BALANCE;
```

The two report views only choose the right account-name column and the columns of each report; the 23 / 19 report columns keep the names of `specs.md` section 7 (aliases).

```sql
CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW APPLICATION.GENERAL_LEDGER.IRP_ENTRY AS
SELECT FUND_NUMBER, FUND_NAME AS SUBFUND_NAME, FUND_CCY AS SUBFUND_CCY,
       FUND_NUMBER AS SUBFUND_NUMBER,
       ACCOUNT_NUMBER, ACCOUNT_RUBRIC, ACCOUNT_NAME_FUND_PLAN AS ACCOUNT_NAME, ACCOUNT_CCY,
       DEBIT_CREDIT, CODE_SERVICE, OPERATION_CODE, ACCOUNTING_DATE, TRADE_DATE, VALUE_DATE, MATURITY_DATE,
       DESCRIPTION, ENTRY, ENTRY_PTF, ENTRY_NEXT, AMOUNT_ACCOUNT_CCY, AMOUNT_SUBFUND_CCY,
       PREVIOUS_BALANCE_ACCOUNT_CCY, BALANCE_ACCOUNT_CCY, STATUS,
       N_LOT, N_LINE, PTF_MANAGER,                               -- technical, for the controls
       IS_RESULT_ACCOUNT, TRADE_DATE_FILTER,                     -- filter columns
       SORT_ACCOUNT, SORT_RUBRIC, SORT_NEXT, SORT_LOT, SORT_LINE, SORT_AMOUNT   -- order columns
FROM BUSINESS.GENERAL_LEDGER.ENTRY;

CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW APPLICATION.GENERAL_LEDGER.BCR_ENTRY AS
SELECT FUND_NUMBER, FUND_NAME AS SUBFUND_NAME, FUND_CCY AS SUBFUND_CCY,
       FUND_NUMBER AS SUBFUND_NUMBER,
       ACCOUNT_NUMBER, ACCOUNT_RUBRIC, ACCOUNT_NAME_BCR_PLAN AS ACCOUNT_NAME, ACCOUNT_CCY,
       DEBIT_CREDIT, CODE_SERVICE, OPERATION_CODE, ACCOUNTING_DATE, TRADE_DATE, VALUE_DATE,
       DESCRIPTION, ENTRY, ENTRY_PTF, AMOUNT_ACCOUNT_CCY, AMOUNT_SUBFUND_CCY, STATUS,
       PREVIOUS_BALANCE_ACCOUNT_CCY, BALANCE_ACCOUNT_CCY, ENTRY_NEXT, MATURITY_DATE,   -- not in the BCR file, kept for the controls
       N_LOT, N_LINE, PTF_MANAGER,
       TRADE_DATE_FILTER,
       SORT_ACCOUNT, SORT_RUBRIC, SORT_ENTRY, SORT_ENTRY_PTF, SORT_LOT, SORT_LINE, SORT_AMOUNT, SORT_NEXT
FROM BUSINESS.GENERAL_LEDGER.ENTRY;
```

## 6. What the application runs

`:x` marks a value from the user's input (see `specs.md` section 1) or from a previous result. Dates are written `DATE 'YYYY-MM-DD'`, funds `'242013'`.

### 6.1 Always

**A1 â€” fund sheet**

```sql
SELECT * FROM APPLICATION.GENERAL_LEDGER.FUND WHERE FUND_NUMBER = :fund
```

No row â†’ unknown fund. `IS_EFRONT = 1` â†’ refuse the fund. Name and currency also come from here.

### 6.2 Window (one of)

**W1 â€” IRP, one NAV, with `nav_date`**

```sql
SELECT * FROM APPLICATION.GENERAL_LEDGER.PERIOD_WINDOW
WHERE FUND_NUMBER = :fund AND NAV_DATE = :nav AND PERIOD_CODE = :period
```

No row â†’ the fund has no lot for this NAV. Gives `LOT_FROM`, `LOT_TO`, `TRADE_DATE_MAX`, `RESULT_LOT_FROM`, `RESULT_DATE_FROM`.

**W0 â€” IRP with `calc_date` (run before W1 to get `:nav`)**

```sql
SELECT NAV_DATE FROM APPLICATION.GENERAL_LEDGER.NAV_CALENDAR
WHERE FUND_NUMBER = :fund AND CALENDAR_TYPE = 'LOTS'
  AND NAV_DATE <= :calc AND CALC_DATE <= :calc
ORDER BY NAV_DATE DESC LIMIT 1
```

**W2 â€” IRP range and BCR `plage`** (two lookups: the NAV in force at `date_to` and at `date_from`)

```sql
SELECT * FROM APPLICATION.GENERAL_LEDGER.NAV_CALENDAR
WHERE FUND_NUMBER = :fund AND CALENDAR_TYPE = 'LOTS'
  AND NAV_DATE <= :date_to AND NEXT_NAV_DATE > :date_to          -- row "TO"

SELECT * FROM APPLICATION.GENERAL_LEDGER.NAV_CALENDAR
WHERE FUND_NUMBER = :fund AND CALENDAR_TYPE = 'LOTS'
  AND NAV_DATE <= :date_from AND NEXT_NAV_DATE > :date_from      -- row "FROM"
```

Window = `LOT_FROM` from row FROM's `LOT_START` (`0` if no row), `LOT_TO` from row TO's `LOT_END`, `TRADE_DATE_MAX` from row TO. No TO row â†’ error "no NAV on or before `date_to`".

**W3 â€” BCR `last_available_day`** (one lookup; the previous NAV's lot bound is already in the row)

```sql
SELECT * FROM APPLICATION.GENERAL_LEDGER.NAV_CALENDAR
WHERE FUND_NUMBER = :fund AND CALENDAR_TYPE = 'CONTROLLED'
  AND NAV_DATE <= :today AND NEXT_NAV_DATE > :today
```

Window = `LOT_FROM` from `PREV_LOT_START`, `LOT_TO` from `LOT_END`, `TRADE_DATE_MAX`. No row, or `PREV_NAV_DATE` null â†’ error.

**W4 â€” BCR `to_last_date_nav`** (two lookups)

```sql
SELECT * FROM APPLICATION.GENERAL_LEDGER.NAV_CALENDAR
WHERE FUND_NUMBER = :fund AND CALENDAR_TYPE = 'PUBLISHED'
  AND NAV_DATE <= :today AND NEXT_NAV_DATE > :today              -- row "TO"

SELECT * FROM APPLICATION.GENERAL_LEDGER.NAV_CALENDAR
WHERE FUND_NUMBER = :fund AND CALENDAR_TYPE = 'PUBLISHED'
  AND PREV_NAV_KEY < :x AND NAV_DATE >= :x                       -- row "FROM", x = LEAST(date_from, row TO NAV_DATE)
```

Window = `LOT_FROM` from row FROM's `LOT_START`, `LOT_TO` from row TO's `LOT_END`, `TRADE_DATE_MAX` from row TO. A missing row â†’ error.

### 6.3 Entries

**E1 â€” IRP**

```sql
SELECT * FROM APPLICATION.GENERAL_LEDGER.IRP_ENTRY
WHERE FUND_NUMBER = :fund
  AND N_LOT > :lot_from AND N_LOT <= :lot_to
  AND TRADE_DATE_FILTER <= :trade_date_max
  AND (IS_RESULT_ACCOUNT = 0 OR (N_LOT > :result_lot_from AND ACCOUNTING_DATE > :result_date_from))   -- single-NAV windows only
  AND ACCOUNT_NUMBER >= :acc_from                                                                     -- only if given
  AND ACCOUNT_NUMBER <= :acc_to                                                                       -- only if given
ORDER BY SORT_ACCOUNT, SORT_RUBRIC, ACCOUNT_CCY, CAST(ACCOUNTING_DATE AS DATE),
         SORT_NEXT, SORT_LOT, SORT_LINE, SORT_AMOUNT, DEBIT_CREDIT
```

**E2 â€” BCR**

```sql
SELECT * FROM APPLICATION.GENERAL_LEDGER.BCR_ENTRY
WHERE FUND_NUMBER = :fund
  AND N_LOT > :lot_from AND N_LOT <= :lot_to
  AND TRADE_DATE_FILTER <= :trade_date_max
  AND ACCOUNT_NUMBER >= :acc_from AND ACCOUNT_NUMBER <= :acc_to        -- default 1450 / 999999
ORDER BY SORT_ACCOUNT, SORT_RUBRIC, ACCOUNT_CCY, CAST(ACCOUNTING_DATE AS DATE),
         SORT_ENTRY, SORT_ENTRY_PTF, SORT_LOT, SORT_LINE, SORT_AMOUNT, SORT_NEXT, DEBIT_CREDIT
```

The `ORDER BY` list is a constant of the application, one per report; the columns it uses are all produced by the business layer.

### 6.4 Control (optional)

**C1 â€” final balances**

```sql
SELECT * FROM APPLICATION.GENERAL_LEDGER.POSITION_BALANCE
WHERE FUND_NUMBER = :fund AND N_LOT = :lot_to
```

### 6.5 Sequence per request

| Request | Statements, in order |
|---|---|
| IRP, `nav_date`, any period | A1 â†’ W1 â†’ E1 â†’ C1 |
| IRP, `calc_date` | A1 â†’ W0 â†’ W1 â†’ E1 â†’ C1 |
| IRP, range | A1 â†’ W2 â†’ E1 â†’ C1 |
| BCR `plage` | A1 â†’ W2 â†’ E2 â†’ C1 |
| BCR `last_available_day` | A1 â†’ W3 â†’ E2 â†’ C1 |
| BCR `to_last_date_nav` | A1 â†’ W4 â†’ E2 â†’ C1 |

Today a period-13 IRP takes up to 6 chained queries with logic in each (Q00, Q02, Q12, Q20, Q35, Q51). Here it takes 4 statements and none of them contains a rule.

## 7. Old query â†’ new object

| Today (`specs.md`) | Becomes | Where the logic now lives |
|---|---|---|
| Q00 fund sheet | A1 on `FUND` | `BUSINESS.FUND` (eFront and backdated flags) |
| Q01 calc date â†’ NAV | W0 on `NAV_CALENDAR` | `BUSINESS.NAV_CALENDAR.CALC_DATE` |
| Q02 last closing | `FUND_CLOSING` + `NAV_LAST_CLOSING` | business views; consumed inside `PERIOD_WINDOW`, never queried by the application |
| Q10, Q11, Q12, Q13, Q14, Q16 window queries | W1 on `PERIOD_WINDOW` | `BUSINESS.PERIOD_WINDOW` (all 16 period rules, corrected rule for 13 and 16) |
| Q15 date-range window | W2 on `NAV_CALENDAR` | validity interval + `LOT_START` / `LOT_END` in `BUSINESS.NAV_CALENDAR` |
| Q18 BCR window from the NAV table | W3 / W4 on `NAV_CALENDAR` | `CONTROLLED` / `PUBLISHED` calendars in `BUSINESS.NAV_CALENDAR` |
| Q20 entries | E1 / E2 on `IRP_ENTRY` / `BCR_ENTRY` | `BUSINESS.ENTRY` (names, previous balance, result flag, trade-date rule, sort keys) |
| Q35 final balances | C1 on `POSITION_BALANCE` | `BUSINESS.POSITION_BALANCE` |
| Q51 latest NAV (history note) | `SELECT NAV_DATE FROM APPLICATION.GENERAL_LEDGER.NAV_CALENDAR WHERE CALENDAR_TYPE = 'LOTS' ORDER BY NAV_DATE DESC LIMIT 1` | `BUSINESS.NAV_CALENDAR` (across all funds; add a `LAST_NAV` view if this proves heavy) |

### 7.1 What is left in the application

Deliberately very little, each item a one-liner:

- refuse the fund if `IS_EFRONT = 1`;
- pass the values of one result to the next `WHERE` (nav, lot window, closing values);
- for W2 and W4, take `LOT_START` of one row and `LOT_END` of another (these two ranges depend on user dates and cannot be precomputed as rows);
- `x = LEAST(date_from, TO.NAV_DATE)` in W4;
- one constant `ORDER BY` list per report;
- `:today` (the run date) for the BCR NAV-table modes;
- the output file serialisation (out of scope here).

---

## 8. Differences, risks and open points

**Behaviour to prove equal.** Run the old query chain and the new statements side by side on the reference cases (fund 242013 IRP period 1 on 2026-06-29; fund 280287 BCR 2026-06-21 â†’ 2026-07-01), then on a backdated-NAV fund (280499), a fund with an annual closing (periods 13, 14, 16), and each of the 16 periods. The row-for-row comparison and the existing control checks of `specs.md` 6.2 are the acceptance test. The 15 measurements already kept in `sql/mesures/gold/` are a ready base.

**Known deviations**

1. **Closing detection (Q02).** The new `FUND_CLOSING` looks at all lots of a fund; the current Q02 only reads the lots up to the requested NAV. The existing note in `sql/02_derniere_cloture.sql` says LUXIS itself does not bound the lots, so the new view follows LUXIS more closely, but a result can differ when a later lot replays an accounting day of a closing.
2. **Trade-date filter.** `TRADE_DATE_FILTER` returns `1900-01-01` for non-backdated funds, so a null trade date is never dropped for them. For backdated funds a null `D_TRADE` is dropped, as today.
3. **The `NAV_CALENDAR` start NAV in `PERIOD_WINDOW`** is looked up only among NAVs up to the requested NAV, as in the current queries.

**Performance â€” to measure before committing.**

- Business views are **views, not tables** (see `docs/CHAINAGE-DONNEES.md` Â§1). The window functions in `NAV_CALENDAR`, `NAV_LAST_CLOSING` and `PERIOD_WINDOW` run per statement. They are cheap when `FUND_NUMBER` is filtered (it is the partition key, so the filter is pushed down) and expensive otherwise. Candidate for a **Dremio reflection** on `NAV_CALENDAR`, `FUND_CLOSING` and `PERIOD_WINDOW`.
- `PERIOD_WINDOW` stacks 16 periods, so it is roughly 16 Ã— (funds Ã— NAVs) rows if ever scanned unfiltered. Always query it by fund and NAV.
- `ENTRY` joins the small `FUND`, `FUND_PLAN`, `ACCOUNT_NAME` views to a table of about 10 million rows. The current Q20 measured that a join with Table Fonds turned a 7 s query into 200+ s, so name and currency were moved into scalar sub-queries. If the same happens here, put `FUND_NAME` and `FUND_CCY` back as scalar sub-queries inside `ENTRY`, or let the application take them from `A1`.
- The `ORDER BY` on `IRP_ENTRY` / `BCR_ENTRY` runs after the filter, on one fund's window, as today.
- Still true on Dremio: avoid literal `IN (â€¦)` lists and joins on `VALUES`; the views above use semi-joins (`EXISTS`) and `UNION ALL`.

**Platform dependencies (from `docs/CHAINAGE-DONNEES.md` Â§8 and Â§10).**

- A **staging replica of the DWH `AMS_CASH_MVT`** (with the lot column) does not exist today; the existing `BUSINESS.FUND_ACCOUNTING.GENERAL_LEDGERS` view cannot be reused (reads `HMT` without lots, and filters on the last 90 days of the technical creation date, so its population changes every day). The new `ENTRY` view has **no date filter** and its population is stable.
- `TAB_FND_MAIN` and `NAV` replicas must exist on **both** INTG and CTLQ; the `BUSINESS` copy of the fund table is missing on CTLQ today. The layers must hold the same objects on both servers, otherwise the report fails at run time.
- Table Fonds and the NAV table are still LUXIS data republished. This design gives the layering and the contract; it does not make the report independent of LUXIS.

**Decisions to take**

1. Names of the spaces and folder (`GENERAL_LEDGER`) and of the views.
2. Who owns the business views (they carry the rules: closing, corrected periods 13 and 16, backdated NAV, chart `'20'`, threshold 40000).
3. Whether eFront funds are refused in the application (as above) or filtered out of `APPLICATIONâ€¦FUND`.
4. Whether the two-lookup windows (W2, W4) are acceptable in the application, or whether a dedicated route is wanted for ranges (which would need a parameterised object, not a plain view).

## 6. Lecture seule : quatre barriÃ¨res

1. Les paramÃ¨tres sont validÃ©s et typÃ©s avant le rendu ; un marqueur n'accepte qu'un fonds, une date, un entier ou une table de la source.
2. Le rendu refuse tout point-virgule et tout marqueur non rÃ©solu.

## 8. Pourquoi le Grand livre ne peut pas passer au gold aujourd'hui

### Blocage A, le filtre de 90 jours porte sur l'horodatage technique

`BUSINESS.FUND_ACCOUNTING.GENERAL_LEDGERS` est dÃ©fini ainsi (**Source** :
`_private\kb\registry\dremio\views.md`) :

```sql
SELECT * from STAGGING.LDR.CORE.AMS.HMT HMT
where HMT.dcreate >= CURRENT_DATE - INTERVAL '90' DAY
order by HMT.djournal asc
```

`DCREATE` est l'horodatage d'Ã©criture technique, pas la date comptable (`DJOURNAL`). La mesure du Â§7
le confirme : les dates comptables couvrent quatorze ans, les horodatages d'Ã©criture trois mois
glissants. ConsÃ©quences :

- la population change **chaque jour** : un Grand livre tirÃ© de cette vue n'est pas reproductible, ce
  qui est inacceptable pour un rapport rÃ©glementaire rejouÃ© Ã  l'identique ;
- sur les **deux** serveurs, le cas de rÃ©fÃ©rence du projet (242013, NAV du 29/06/2026, pÃ©riode 1) est
  **introuvable** : q3 rend zÃ©ro ligne gold pour juin 2026 contre 3 905 lignes brutes, sur CTLQ comme
  sur INTG (Â§7). Les 6 247 lignes visibles sur CTLQ et les 2 037 sur INTG sont celles des trois
  derniers mois d'Ã©criture technique, pas celles de la pÃ©riode demandÃ©e ;
- le filtre ne gÃ¨le pas avec le serveur. Une version antÃ©rieure de ce document affirmait que la vue
  rendait zÃ©ro ligne sur INTG, par raisonnement Ã  partir de la copie arrÃªtÃ©e au 03/07/2026. **C'est
  faux** : q1 y mesure 570 846 lignes et 233 fonds, avec `DCREATE` jusqu'au 06/10/2026. La vue lit
  MFGA CORE en direct, pas le datamart gelÃ©. D'oÃ¹ le blocage E.

### Blocage B, la source gold des Ã©critures n'a pas de numÃ©ro de lot

`GENERAL_LEDGERS` lit `STAGGING.LDR.CORE.AMS.HMT`, les Ã©critures de MFGA **CORE**, alors que
l'application lit `AMS_CASH_MVT`, le datamart **DWH**. Les 43 colonnes de `HMT` ne portent **aucune
colonne de lot**. La fenÃªtre du Grand livre, `N_LOT > LOT_FROM AND N_LOT <= LOT_TO`, n'y est donc pas
exprimable : il faudrait rÃ©Ã©crire toute la sÃ©lection des Ã©critures sur des dates, et revalider
entiÃ¨rement le rÃ©sultat contre LUXIS. Ce n'est pas un repointage de table, c'est une rÃ©Ã©criture.

### Blocage C, `APPLICATION` n'ajoute rien

## 4. Le rendu du SQL : trois garde-fous dans un module de 161 lignes

`glapp\sqlrender.py` est petit et il est le cÅ“ur de la sÃ©curitÃ© en lecture seule.

- `{{NOM}}` est un marqueur **typÃ©** : `KINDS` dit si c'est un fonds, une date, un entier, une liste

## 1. En bref

Un **pool** est un fonds qui porte les positions et les Ã©critures comptables de plusieurs **feeders**, qui n'en dÃ©tiennent qu'une quote-part. **DÃ©pooler** une structure, c'est la dÃ©faire : les classes de parts quittent les feeders et passent sous le pool, qui devient un fonds ordinaire.

**Convention 2026, retenue par le Reporting le 02/10/2026 : le pool garde son numÃ©ro** et reprend les classes de ses feeders. Les feeders cessent de produire. 2. **le rapport du pool**, sous le numÃ©ro du fonds qui reste, **Ã  partir du lot de transfert**, c'est-Ã -dire du lot MFGA du pool pour la NAV du jour du depooling.

Chaque rapport est un Grand livre ordinaire de 23 colonnes, avec ses propres fichiers (CSV et classeur au nom de LUXIS, CSV brut, JSON) dans son propre dossier. Ces fichiers-lÃ , les seuls Ã  porter un contrÃ´le et un verdict, n'ont **ni colonne Â« Fonds d'origine Â» ni feuille annexe**.

**Depuis le 08/10/2026, Ã  la demande du Reporting**, un **troisiÃ¨me fichier**, `<tag du pool>_avant_apres_depooling` (`.csv` et `.xlsx`), est produit automatiquement Ã  cÃ´tÃ© des deux rapports dÃ¨s qu'il y a au moins un ancien feeder : il rÃ©unit, pour l'envoi, les Ã©critures d'avant et d'aprÃ¨s depooling dans un seul fichier (CSV : les lignes des feeders puis celles du pool, avec une colonne technique Â« Fonds d'origine Â» ; XLSX : feuille Â« A Â» = le pool, feuille annexe Â« Avant depooling Â» = les feeders). **Ce fichier est un confort pour l'envoi, pas une troisiÃ¨me preuve** : il ne porte ni contrÃ´le ni verdict propres, et le reconstruire soi-mÃªme en sommant les deux Grands livres rÃ©introduirait le double compte dÃ©crit ci-dessus. ## 4. Ce que fait l'application

### Les rapports

## 6. Comment lire les rapports

- Le **rapport du pool** commence au lot de transfert : il ne contient rien d'avant. L'historique d'avant est dans les rapports des anciens feeders, chacun sous son numÃ©ro.
- Pour reconstituer l'historique du fonds qui reste, lire les rapports **l'un aprÃ¨s l'autre**, sans les additionner : au lot de transfert, le pool reprend les soldes de rÃ©sultat du feeder, qui seraient comptÃ©s deux fois dans une somme.
- Le chaÃ®nage des soldes est rompu entre le feeder et le pool, par construction. Les contrÃ´les d'Ã©quilibre et de chaÃ®nage valent **par rapport**.
- Chaque rapport est dans la devise de son fonds, sans conversion.

Ã‰tapes : `02_derniere_cloture` (NAV de clÃ´ture), `12_fenetre_p13` (fenÃªtre du code 13), `13_fenetre_p14` (fenÃªtre du code 14), `20_ecritures` (lignes de chaque code), `60_ecart_13_16` (nature des lignes non reprises). ### 02_derniere_cloture

```sql
WITH t AS (
  SELECT c.N_LOT, c.N_ENTRY, c.D_ACC, c.C_N_ACC, c.C_SRV, c.R_EXCHANGE, c.C_STATUS
  FROM "MFGA_INFOCENTRE"."DWH"."AMS_CASH_MVT" c
  WHERE c.C_FUND = '313374' AND c.C_SRV = 'RS'
    AND c.N_LOT IN (SELECT l.N_LOT FROM "MFGA_INFOCENTRE"."DWH"."AMS_LOT" l WHERE l.C_FUND = '313374' AND l.D_NAV <= TIMESTAMP '2026-05-31 00:00:00')),
rs AS (
  SELECT t.* FROM t
  WHERE t.C_N_ACC >= 40000 AND t.C_N_ACC NOT IN (47410, 57410, 999998) AND t.R_EXCHANGE <> 0 AND t.C_STATUS = 20),
maxlot AS (SELECT t.D_ACC, t.C_N_ACC, MAX(t.N_LOT) AS ML FROM t GROUP BY t.D_ACC, t.C_N_ACC),
rev AS (SELECT DISTINCT t.C_N_ACC, t.N_ENTRY FROM t WHERE t.C_STATUS = 30),
cand AS (
  SELECT rs.N_LOT, rs.D_ACC FROM rs
  JOIN maxlot m ON m.D_ACC = rs.D_ACC AND m.C_N_ACC = rs.C_N_ACC AND m.ML = rs.N_LOT
  LEFT JOIN rev r ON r.C_N_ACC = rs.C_N_ACC AND r.N_ENTRY = rs.N_ENTRY
  WHERE r.N_ENTRY IS NULL),
lots AS (SELECT l.N_LOT, l.D_NAV FROM "MFGA_INFOCENTRE"."DWH"."AMS_LOT" l WHERE l.C_FUND = '313374'),
clot AS (SELECT c.N_LOT AS LOT_RS, MAX(l.N_LOT) AS LOT_CLOT FROM cand c JOIN lots l ON l.N_LOT < c.N_LOT GROUP BY c.N_LOT)
SELECT k.LOT_RS, k.LOT_CLOT, l.D_NAV AS DATE_NAV_CLOT
FROM clot k JOIN lots l ON l.N_LOT = k.LOT_CLOT
WHERE l.D_NAV < TIMESTAMP '2026-05-31 00:00:00'
ORDER BY k.LOT_RS DESC
LIMIT 1
```

### 12_fenetre_p13 (code 13, rÃ¨gle LUXIS)

```sql
WITH cal AS (
  SELECT l.D_NAV, MIN(l.N_LOT) AS LOT_MIN, MAX(l.N_LOT) AS LOT_MAX
  FROM "MFGA_INFOCENTRE"."DWH"."AMS_LOT" l
  WHERE l.C_FUND = '313374' AND l.D_NAV <= TIMESTAMP '2026-05-31 00:00:00'
  GROUP BY l.D_NAV),
fonds AS (
  SELECT CASE WHEN COALESCE(MAX(CAST(t.NAV_BACKDATED AS INTEGER)), 2) <> 2 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS BACKDATED
  FROM "LUXIS"."REPADMIN"."TAB_FND_MAIN" t WHERE t.FA_NUM = '313374'),
debut AS (
  SELECT MIN(c.D_NAV) AS NAV_FROM FROM cal c WHERE c.D_NAV > TIMESTAMP '2025-09-30 00:00:00' AND c.D_NAV <= TIMESTAMP '2026-05-31 00:00:00'
  )
SELECT a.D_NAV AS NAV_TO, d.NAV_FROM AS NAV_FROM,
       COALESCE(CASE WHEN f.BACKDATED = 1 THEN b.LOT_MIN ELSE b.LOT_MAX END, 0) AS LOT_FROM,
       a.LOT_MAX AS LOT_TO,
       CASE WHEN f.BACKDATED = 1 THEN a.D_NAV END AS TRADE_DATE_MAX,
       CAST(NULL AS BIGINT) AS LOT_RESULT_FROM
FROM cal a
CROSS JOIN debut d
CROSS JOIN fonds f
LEFT JOIN cal b ON b.D_NAV = d.NAV_FROM
WHERE a.D_NAV = TIMESTAMP '2026-05-31 00:00:00'
```

## 2. Comment c'est fait

- **ModÃ¨les SQL avec drapeau**, dans le style de `sql\` : le drapeau `SANS_LUXIS` choisit, dans `00_fonds`, `10` Ã  `17`, `20`, `40` et `44`, le bloc MFGA ; le bloc LUXIS est inchangÃ©. - Valeurs posÃ©es par `glapp\sansluxis.py` Ã  partir des tables figÃ©es : `{{ANTIDATE}}` (1 ou 0) remplace la lecture de `NAV_BACKDATED` ; `{{FIRST_NAV}}` (drapeau `PREMIERE_NAV_FIXE`) ou `PREMIERE_NAV_AUCUNE` (lot 0) remplace la premiÃ¨re NAV MFGA des fonds en Ã©cart ; `{{CCY}}` (drapeau `DEVISE_FIXE`, trois lettres majuscules vÃ©rifiÃ©es) remplace la devise MFGA des fonds en Ã©cart. - Tous les fonds d'une NAV : l'Ã©tape 44 rend la fiche MFGA et la fenÃªtre du code 1 sans antidate ; un fonds de la liste `nav_antidatee` voit sa fenÃªtre recalculÃ©e par l'Ã©tape 10 avec le drapeau (aucun au 29/06/2026).
- `--sans-luxis` ne se combine pas avec `--source lx` (copie LUXIS). Le nom du dossier de sortie reÃ§oit le suffixe `_sansluxis` ; les fichiers au nom de LUXIS gardent leur nom.
